_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-04 19:08:12Z)**_

Here are some verbs in the same spirit, each with how it would look as a command:

**Light it up**
- **illuminate**: clear and literal, but 10 letters is a lot to type (`illuminate "how does signup work?"`)
- **illume**: the old poetic form of illuminate. Shorter and less common.
- **kindle**: to start a light. It's also the Amazon e-reader, which could confuse people.
- **glimmer**: friendly, though it sounds a bit faint for a tool that checks its claims.

**Reveal it**
- **reveal**: plain, and it says what the tool does
- **unveil**: you pull the cover off code you didn't write
- **surface**: as in bringing hidden things to the surface. Very common word, though.

**Guide the way**
- **lead**, **beckon**, **guide**: probably too generic to stand out

**Spell verbs** (verbs in Latin, if you still want the pop-culture angle)
- **lumos**: "light!"
- **revelio**: "reveal!"

My pick is **illuminate**, with **illume** as the short form for the CLI. That keeps the meaning you liked and stays easy to type. If one name has to cover everything, I'd go with **reveal** or **lumos**.

Tell me which one, and I'll rename the packages, the CLI, the skill and the docs, then run the tests and typecheck.

One more choice: should saved maps move from `.codemap/` to the new folder name? That would orphan maps already saved in repos you've used it on, unless I also keep reading the old folder.

```text
// Maps on disk, in the target repo: `.codemap/maps/<id>.json`. Commit them to share; teammates re-check them against
// their own copy of the code when they open them. Each file also keeps the questions asked on the map with their
// answers, and where each proposed fix stands, so a reopened map still has its conversation.
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { parseMap, slugify, type CodeMap } from '@codemap/core';
import type { Answer } from './explainer';

export type MapMeta = {
  id: string;
  question: string;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  commit: string | null;
  makerSession: string | null;
  explainerSession: string | null;
  cost: number;
  /** The map this one was started from, when a question there turned out to be about something else. */
  parent?: { mapId: string; question: string } | null;
};
/** Where a proposed fix stands. Undo isn't saved: it needs the files as they were, which only the running server has. */
export type SavedFix = { status: 'proposed' | 'applied' | 'rejected'; edgeId?: string | null; closed?: string[] };
export type StoredMap = { meta: MapMeta; map: CodeMap; answers?: Answer[]; fixes?: Record<string, SavedFix> };

const ID = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,80}$/;

export function createStore(root: string) {
  const base = path.join(root, '.codemap');
  const dir = path.join(base, 'maps');

  const ensure = () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    const ignore = path.join(base, '.gitignore');
    // Maps are worth committing; scratch output is not.
    if (!fs.existsSync(ignore)) fs.writeFileSync(ignore, 'fixes/\nws-modules/\n');
  };
  const file = (id: string) => {
    if (!ID.test(id)) throw new Error(`Not a map id: ${id}`);
    return path.join(dir, `${id}.json`);
  };

  return {
    dir,
    get(id: string): StoredMap | null {
      let raw: { meta?: MapMeta; map?: unknown; answers?: unknown; fixes?: unknown };
      try {
        raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file(id), 'utf8'));
      } catch {
        return null;
      }

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Runs the TypeScript CLI directly (no build step) through tsx's loader.
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import { register } from 'tsx/esm/api';

// Codemap's own settings (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CODEMAP_MODEL) from a .env at the codemap checkout's root. This is never
// the target repo's .env, which codemap refuses to read. Variables already set in the shell win, and empty ones are
// skipped so a blank key doesn't hide a Claude Code login.
const envFile = new URL('../../../.env', import.meta.url);
if (existsSync(envFile)) {
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(parseEnv(readFileSync(envFile, 'utf8')))) {
    if (value && process.env[key] === undefined) process.env[key] = value;
  }
}

register();
await import('../src/cli.ts');

## Notes

- illuminate reads the code and never changes it, except for a fix the user approves in the map.
- It never reads secret files (`.env`, keys) and only listens on 127.0.0.1.
- It needs Claude access: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code.

const ID = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,80}$/;

export function createStore(root: string) {
  const base = path.join(root, '.illuminate');
  const dir = path.join(base, 'maps');

  const ensure = () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    const ignore = path.join(base, '.gitignore');
    // Maps are worth committing; scratch output is not.
    if (!fs.existsSync(ignore)) fs.writeFileSync(ignore, 'fixes/\nws-modules/\n');
  };
  const file = (id: string) => {
    if (!ID.test(id)) throw new Error(`Not a map id: ${id}`);
    return path.join(dir, `${id}.json`);
  };

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

.card-ok { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ok) 55%, var(--line)); }
.card-dead { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--dead) 55%, var(--line)); }
.card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.3; font-weight: 650; text-wrap: balance; }
.card p { margin: 0; }
.tabs { display: flex; gap: 2px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
.tab { border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 6px 9px; cursor: pointer; color: var(--muted); border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; margin-bottom: -1px; font-size: 13px; }

.depths { display: grid; gap: 8px; }

.chips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
.chip { display: inline-flex; gap: 5px; align-items: center; font-size: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--surface); border-radius: 999px; padding: 3px 9px; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; }
.chip.static { cursor: default; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 11.5px; }
.chip-unconfirmed { border-style: dashed; color: var(--muted); }
.tick { color: var(--ok); font-weight: 700; }
.qmark { color: var(--muted); font-weight: 700; }
.basis { display: grid; gap: 6px; }
.progress { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 5px; font-size: 13px; }
.progress li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 16px 1fr; gap: 6px; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.progress .ic { color: var(--ok); font-weight: 700; }
.progress .running, .progress .running .ic { color: var(--ai); }
.btns, .tour-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
.btn { border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--surface); border-radius: 7px; padding: 7px 11px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; }
.btn:hover { border-color: var(--accent); }
a.btn { display: inline-block; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink); }
.btn.primary { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--surface); }
.btn:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }
.diff { margin: 0; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; font: 11.5px/1.55 var(--mono); overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre; max-height: 260px; }
.diff .add { color: var(--ok); }
.diff .del { color: var(--dead); }
.diff .file { color: var(--muted); font-weight: 600; }
.warn { color: var(--ai); }
.problems { margin: 0; padding-left: 1.1em; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--muted); display: grid; gap: 4px; }
.problems-box summary { cursor: pointer; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--muted); }
.dots { display: flex; gap: 6px; }
.dots i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--line); }
.dots i.done { background: var(--accent-soft); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent); }
.dots i.on { background: var(--accent); width: 20px; border-radius: 4px; }
.kbd { font: 11px var(--mono); color: var(--muted); }
.history { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 4px; }
.layers { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 6px; }
.layers label { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; cursor: pointer; }
.layer-n { font: 500 11px/1.3 var(--mono); color: var(--accent); min-width: 2.5ch; }
.layer-q { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; min-width: 0; }
.link-btn { border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 0; color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer; text-align: left; font-size: 13px; }
.link-btn.on { font-weight: 600; }
.banner { border-radius: 10px; padding: 9px 12px; font-size: 13px; display: flex; gap: 10px; justify-content: space-between; align-items: start; }
.banner-dead { background: var(--dead-soft); color: var(--dead); border: 1px solid var(--dead); }

/* ---------- home ---------- */
.home { max-width: 760px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 56px 20px 80px; display: grid; gap: 18px; }
.home h1 { margin: 0; font-size: clamp(28px, 4vw, 38px); letter-spacing: -0.015em; line-height: 1.1; }
.lede { font-size: 16px; margin: 0; }
.home-ask { display: flex; gap: 8px; }

.section-title { font-size: 13px; margin: 18px 0 8px; color: var(--muted); font-weight: 600; }
.maplist { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 8px; }
.maplist li { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; padding: 11px 14px; display: grid; gap: 2px; }
.maplist a { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }
.maplist a:hover { color: var(--accent); }
.home-foot { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding-top: 16px; margin-top: 8px; }
// The map format: what Claude (or later the engine) writes, the checker verifies and the viewer draws.
// This is the one-way door. Statuses are never part of it: the checker computes them from the repo every time.
import { z } from 'zod';

const Id = z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$/, 'ids use letters, digits, _ . : - (at most 64)');

/** A line of code that backs a claim. `text` must appear on that line (whitespace-insensitive) or within a few lines of it. */
export const Evidence = z.object({
  file: z.string().min(1),
  line: z.number().int().positive(),
  text: z.string().min(1).max(400),
});

/** How a box is drawn: a way in (button, route, CLI), a step, a store (table, queue), something outside the repo, a job. */
export const NodeKind = z.enum(['entry', 'step', 'store', 'external', 'job']);

/**
 * What an arrow claims. `calls`, `request` (fetch → route) and `imports` are also proven from code facts;
 * `then` (and anything the extractors can't see yet, like events) is proven by its evidence text alone.
 */
export const EdgeKind = z.enum(['calls', 'request', 'imports', 'then']);

export const Area = z.object({ id: Id, label: z.string().min(1).max(40) });

export const Node = z.object({
  id: Id,
  area: Id,
  kind: NodeKind.default('step'),
  name: z.string().min(1).max(80),
  /** `<file>#<symbol>` as the facts name it, e.g. `src/patients/service.ts#markConverted`. */
  symbol: z.string().regex(/^[^#]+#.+$/, 'symbol is <file>#<name>').optional(),
  explain: z.object({ concept: z.string(), how: z.string(), code: z.string() }).partial().optional(),
  evidence: z.array(Evidence).min(1),
});

export const Edge = z.object({
  id: Id,
  from: Id,
  to: Id,
  kind: EdgeKind.default('then'),
  label: z.string().min(1).max(60),
  evidence: z.array(Evidence).min(1),
});

/** A claim that something is missing, proven by a search the checker runs again: `matches` is the count claimed. */
export const Absence = z.object({
  id: Id,
  claim: z.string().min(1).max(200),
  /** Draw it as a missing arrow between these boxes. */
  between: z.object({ from: Id, to: Id }).optional(),
  search: z.object({
    pattern: z.string().min(1).max(200),
    regex: z.boolean().default(false),
    /** Globs to search; the whole repo when omitted. */
    paths: z.array(z.string().min(1)).optional(),
  }),
  matches: z.number().int().min(0),
});

export const TourStop = z.object({
  id: Id,
  title: z.string().min(1).max(80),
  text: z.string().min(1).max(1200),
  focus: z.object({
    areas: z.array(Id).optional(),
    nodes: z.array(Id).optional(),
    edges: z.array(Id).optional(),
    absences: z.array(Id).optional(),
  }),
  terms: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  ask: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

export const CodeMap = z.object({
  version: z.literal(1),
  question: z.string().min(1).max(300),
  /** The commit the map was made from, when known. */
  commit: z.string().nullable().optional(),
  areas: z.array(Area).min(1),
  nodes: z.array(Node).min(1),
  edges: z.array(Edge).default([]),
  absences: z.array(Absence).default([]),
  tour: z.array(TourStop).default([]),
});

export type Evidence = z.output<typeof Evidence>;
export type MapNode = z.output<typeof Node>;
export type MapEdge = z.output<typeof Edge>;
export type MapAbsence = z.output<typeof Absence>;
export type TourStop = z.output<typeof TourStop>;
export type CodeMap = z.output<typeof CodeMap>;

export type ParseResult = { ok: true; map: CodeMap } | { ok: false; problems: string[] };

/** A repo-relative path that can't climb out of the repo: no absolute paths, no `..`, no backslashes. */
export function isSafeRelativePath(path: string): boolean {
  if (!path || path.startsWith('/') || path.includes('\\') || /^[A-Za-z]:/.test(path)) return false;
  return path.split('/').every((seg) => seg !== '..' && seg !== '');
}

/** Validates shape, then references: unique ids, edges between real boxes, tour stops that point at real things. */
export function parseMap(input: unknown): ParseResult {
  const parsed = CodeMap.safeParse(input);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return { ok: false, problems: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join('.') || '(map)'}: ${i.message}`) };
  }
  const map = parsed.data;
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const ids = (kind: string, items: readonly { id: string }[]) => {
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const { id } of items) {
      if (seen.has(id)) problems.push(`${kind} id "${id}" is used twice`);
      seen.add(id);
    }
    return seen;
  };
  const areas = ids('area', map.areas);
  const nodes = ids('node', map.nodes);
  const edges = ids('edge', map.edges);
  const absences = ids('absence', map.absences);

<script>
const N = {
  s1: { area: 'Patients', kind: 'entry', name: 'Staff clicks Convert', file: 'PatientHeader.tsx' },

  s3: { area: 'Patients', name: 'Patient enrolled', file: 'service.ts' },

  u1: { area: 'Automations', name: 'Check the rules', file: 'evaluate.ts' },
  u2: { area: 'Automations', name: 'Queue the email', file: 'queue.ts' },
  u3: { area: 'Automations', name: 'Send welcome email', file: 'send.ts' },
  j1: { area: 'Background jobs', kind: 'job', name: 'Nightly job, 2:00 am', file: 'nightly.ts' },
};
const E = [['s1','s2','sends request'],['s2','s3','calls'],['s3','s4','announces'],['u1','u2','if a rule matches'],['u2','u3','sends'],['j1','u1','every night']];
const GAP = ['s4','u1'];
const icon = { Patients: ['#e3efe9','#2d7a55','●'], Events: ['#efe8f8','#6b4bb0','◆'], Automations: ['#fdf1d2','#9a6a00','⚙'], 'Background jobs': ['#e6ecf6','#3a5a92','◷'] };

function edgePath(a, b) {
  const [ax, ay, aw, ah] = a, [bx, by, bw, bh] = b;
  if (Math.abs(ay - by) < 2) { const l = ax < bx; return { d: `M${l?ax+aw:ax} ${ay+ah/2} L${l?bx:bx+bw} ${by+bh/2}`, m: [(l?ax+aw+bx:ax+bx+bw)/2, ay+ah/2] }; }
  if (Math.abs(ax - bx) < 2) { const x = ax + aw/2; return { d: `M${x} ${ay+ah} L${x} ${by}`, m: [x, (ay+ah+by)/2] }; }
  const x1 = ax + aw, y1 = ay + ah/2, x2 = bx + bw/2, y2 = by + bh; // right side → up into bottom
  return { d: `M${x1} ${y1} L${x2-14} ${y1} Q${x2} ${y1} ${x2} ${y1-14} L${x2} ${y2}`, m: [(x1+x2)/2, y1] };
}
function arrowDefs(color, id) { return `<marker id="${id}" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M1 1 L9 5 L1 9" fill="none" stroke="${color}" stroke-width="1.6"/></marker>`; }

function build(id, pos, size, nodeHtml, style) {
  const stage = document.querySelector(`#${id} .stage`);
  let svg = `<svg width="${stage.dataset.w}" height="${stage.dataset.h}"><defs>${arrowDefs(style.line,'a'+id)}${arrowDefs(style.gap,'g'+id)}</defs>`;
  let html = '';
  const box = (k) => [pos[k][0], pos[k][1], size[0], size[1]];
  for (const [f, t, label] of E) {
    const p = edgePath(box(f), box(t));
    svg += `<path d="${p.d}" fill="none" stroke="${style.line}" stroke-width="${style.w}" marker-end="url(#a${id})" opacity="${style.dimEdge?.(f,t) ?? 1}"/>`;
    html += `<div class="elabel" style="left:${p.m[0]}px;top:${p.m[1]}px;opacity:${style.dimEdge?.(f,t) ?? ''}">${label}</div>`;
  }
  const g = edgePath(box(GAP[0]), box(GAP[1]));
  svg += `<path d="${g.d}" fill="none" stroke="${style.gap}" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 6" marker-end="url(#g${id})"/>`;
  html += style.gapHtml(g.m);
  for (const k in pos) html += `<div class="node ${nodeHtml.cls(k)}" style="left:${pos[k][0]}px;top:${pos[k][1]}px">${nodeHtml.inner(k)}</div>`;
  stage.innerHTML = svg + '</svg>' + (style.under || '') + html + (style.extra || '');
}

/* A */
const posA = { s1:[40,80], s2:[370,80], s3:[700,80], s4:[1030,80], u3:[370,470], u2:[700,470], u1:[1030,470], j1:[1240,650] };
build('A', { ...posA, j1: undefined } && posA, [238,140], {
  cls: (k) => (N[k].kind === 'job' ? 'job' : '') + (k === 's4' ? ' sel' : ''),
  inner: (k) => { const [bg, fg, ch] = icon[N[k].area]; return `<div class="who"><i style="background:${bg};color:${fg}">${ch}</i>${N[k].area}${N[k].kind==='entry'?', where it starts':''}</div><h3>${N[k].name}</h3><div class="chip"><span class="t">✓</span>${N[k].file}</div>`; },
}, {
  line: '#7d857f', gap: '#cf4a33', w: 1.4,
  gapHtml: ([x, y]) => `<div class="gapq" style="left:${x}px;top:${y}px">?</div><div class="gapnote" style="left:${x+52}px;top:${y}px">Nothing listens for “converted”<small>Searched the whole app: 0 subscribers</small></div>`,
  extra: `<div class="pop" style="left:1290px;top:70px"><div class="bar"><span>Events</span><span>·</span><span>confirmed in service.ts:42</span><button class="x" aria-label="Close">×</button></div><h4>Announces “converted”</h4><div class="tabs"><button class="on">In plain words</button><button>How</button><button>Code</button></div><p>Once the patient is enrolled, the app broadcasts that they converted, so any part of the app that cares can react. Right now, nothing does.</p><div class="reply">Ask about this step<b>↑</b></div></div>`,
});
/* the nightly job sits under "Check the rules"; redraw its edge as vertical by placing it directly below */
posA.j1 = [1030, 690];

/* B */
const lit = new Set(['s3','s4','u1']);
build('B', { s1:[40,70], s2:[370,70], s3:[700,70], s4:[1030,70], u3:[370,400], u2:[700,400], u1:[1030,400], j1:[1290,400] }, [238,112], {
  cls: (k) => lit.has(k) ? 'lit' : '',
  inner: (k) => `<div class="who">${N[k].area}</div><h3>${N[k].name}</h3><div class="file">${N[k].file}</div>`,
}, {
  line: '#5a6782', gap: '#ff7a66', w: 1.4,
  dimEdge: (f, t) => lit.has(f) && lit.has(t) ? 1 : 0.45,
  gapHtml: ([x, y]) => `<div class="elabel gapl" style="left:${x}px;top:${y}px">nothing listens</div>`,
});

/* C: lanes */
const lanes = [['Patients', '#f3f7fd', 0], ['Events', '#f7f4fd', 150], ['Automations', '#f2f9f5', 300], ['Background jobs', '#fbf8f1', 450]];
const posC = { s1:[180,38], s2:[440,38], s3:[700,38], s4:[960,188], u1:[960,338], u2:[700,338], u3:[440,338], j1:[1080,488] };
build('C', posC, [200,74], {
  cls: (k) => [N[k].kind === 'entry' ? 'way' : '', N[k].kind === 'job' ? 'job' : '', ['s4','u1'].includes(k) ? 'focus' : ''].join(' '),
  inner: (k) => `<h3>${N[k].name}</h3><div class="file">${N[k].file}</div>`,
}, {
  line: '#8b95ab', gap: '#d23f2c', w: 1.5,
  gapHtml: ([x, y]) => `<div class="elabel gapl" style="left:${x}px;top:${y}px">nothing listens for “converted”</div>`,
  under: lanes.map(([n, bg, y]) => `<div class="lane" style="top:${y}px;height:150px;width:1300px;background:${bg};border-bottom:1px solid #e9ecf2"><div class="name">${n}</div></div>`).join(''),
});

/* fix the S-curve case in C (s3 → s4 goes down a lane) and j1 → u1 (up-left) by simple elbows: handled by edgePath */

function fit() {
  document.querySelectorAll('.frame.on .stage').forEach((s) => {
    const w = s.parentElement.clientWidth, h = s.parentElement.clientHeight;
    const k = Math.min(w / s.dataset.w, (h - 10) / s.dataset.h, 1.1);
    s.style.transform = `translate(${(w - s.dataset.w * k) / 2}px, ${Math.max(8, (h - 110 - s.dataset.h * k) / 2)}px) scale(${k})`;
  });
}
document.querySelectorAll('.picker button').forEach((b) => b.onclick = () => {
  document.querySelectorAll('.picker button').forEach((x) => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', x === b));
  document.querySelectorAll('.frame').forEach((f) => f.classList.toggle('on', f.id === b.dataset.k));
  fit();
});
addEventListener('resize', fit); fit();
</script>

</html>

The page is open in Chrome at http://127.0.0.1:5391/mockups.html, with buttons at the top to switch between them. It's served from a small local web server I left running; the file is `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnzhang-Documents-GitHub-codemap/528b535b-7e85-49df-892b-e0213fd4828f/scratchpad/mockups.html`. I checked all three in screenshots after fixing two layout problems: a card hidden behind a panel, and arrows hidden under the lanes in C.

All three fix your current toolbar the same way. The top bar keeps only the name, the question, the check status and Stop. Walkthrough, Ask, Pick, Whole map and Find move out of it.

**A · Canvas** (closest to your Zapier reference)
- Big white cards. Each has a small header with an icon and the area name, a large title, and a chip at the bottom showing the file that backs it, ticked when confirmed.
- Arrows are thin, with plain text labels on the line.
- The gap borrows the reference's "?" bubble: a red dashed line with "Nothing listens for 'converted'" and the search that proved it.
- Clicking a box opens a dark popover next to it instead of the side panel, with plain-words / How / Code tabs and an "Ask about this step" field.
- Tools sit in a floating dock at the bottom, in three groups: Walkthrough, Ask about the map, and View.

**B · Lantern** (leans into the name)
- A dark blue canvas where the current walkthrough stop is lit up in warm gold and everything else is dimmed.
- The walkthrough reads like a caption at the bottom left, with a "Show me the fix" button.
- The ask bar becomes "Ask about what's lit…".
- It has the most personality, but at this window size the map shrinks to make room for the caption.

**C · Lanes** (most structured)
- One horizontal band per area: Patients, Events, Automations, Background jobs. You can see at a glance where the flow crosses between parts of the app.
- The walkthrough becomes a numbered story down the left, with the gap stop in red.
- Starting points are pill-shaped, and the nightly job has a dashed border.

My recommendation is A as the base, plus two pieces from the others: B's lit-up walkthrough step (it suits the name and makes the tour obvious) and C's numbered story list as an expandable part of the dock.

```text
// The two screens: the list of maps (with a box to ask a new question), and a map with its panel and input bar. Moving
// between them doesn't reload the page.
import { useCallback, useEffect, useReducer, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { ReactFlowProvider, useReactFlow } from '@xyflow/react';
import { ApiError, api, connect, pageUrl, token } from './api';
import { Composer } from './composer';
import { MapGraph } from './graph';
import { Home } from './home';
import { navigate, usePath } from './nav';
import { StopButton, Stopped } from './stop';
import { Panel } from './panel';
import { addedIds, currentView, initialState, reducer, selSize, visibleMap, type Sel } from './state';
import type { CheckReport } from './types';

export function App() {
  if (!token) {
    return (
      <main className="home">
        <h1>Open illuminate from its link</h1>
        <p className="muted lede">Use the link illuminate printed in your terminal (it ends in <code>?t=…</code>).</p>
      </main>
    );
  }
  return <Screens />;
}

function Screens() {
  const [stopped, setStopped] = useState(false);
  const onStopped = useCallback(() => setStopped(true), []);
  const path = usePath();
  if (stopped) return <Stopped />;
  const m = /^\/m\/([a-z0-9-]{1,80})\/?$/.exec(path);
  return m ? <MapScreen key={m[1]} mapId={m[1]!} onStopped={onStopped} /> : <Home onStopped={onStopped} />;
}

/** Every map in this repo, to jump between, with the current one showing. */
function MapSwitcher({ mapId, question }: { mapId: string; question: string }) {
  const [maps, setMaps] = useState<{ id: string; question: string; making?: boolean }[]>([]);
  useEffect(() => {
    api.list().then(
      (r) => setMaps([...r.making.map((x) => ({ ...x, making: true })), ...r.maps.map((x) => ({ id: x.id, question: x.question }))]),
      () => {},
    );
  }, [mapId]);
  const list = maps.some((x) => x.id === mapId) ? maps : [{ id: mapId, question }, ...maps];
  return (
    <select className="switcher" value={mapId} onChange={(e) => navigate(pageUrl(e.target.value))} aria-label="Switch to another map" title="Switch to another map in this repo">
      {list.map((x) => <option key={x.id} value={x.id}>{x.question || x.id}{x.making ? ' (being made)' : ''}</option>)}
    </select>
  );
}

/** Zoom the map in and out (the mouse wheel and trackpad do the same). */
function ZoomButtons() {
  const rf = useReactFlow();
  return (
    <span className="zoom">
      <button className="tool" aria-label="Zoom out" title="Zoom out" onClick={() => void rf.zoomOut({ duration: 200 })}>−</button>
      <button className="tool" aria-label="Zoom in" title="Zoom in" onClick={() => void rf.zoomIn({ duration: 200 })}>+</button>
    </span>
  );
}

function Summary({ report }: { report: CheckReport | null }) {
  if (!report) return null;
  const { claims, confirmed, unconfirmed } = report.summary;
  return unconfirmed
    ? <span className="summary warn" title="Some claims didn't check out against the code; they're marked with ?">✓ {confirmed} of {claims} confirmed</span>
    : <span className="summary ok" title="Every box and arrow was checked against the code">✓ All {claims} confirmed</span>;
}


function MapScreen({ mapId, onStopped }: { mapId: string; onStopped: () => void }) {
  const [s, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, mapId, initialState);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState('');
  const wasConnected = useRef(false);

  const load = useCallback(() => {
    api.get(mapId).then(
      (payload) => dispatch({ type: 'loaded', payload }),
      (e: Error) => dispatch(e instanceof ApiError && /No such map/.test(e.message) ? { type: 'missing' } : { type: 'error', message: e.message }),
    );
  }, [mapId]);

  useEffect(load, [load]);
  useEffect(
    () =>
      connect(
        (event) => dispatch({ type: 'event', event }),
        (value) => {
          dispatch({ type: 'connected', value });
          if (value && wasConnected.current === false && s.phase !== 'loading') load(); // catch up after a reconnect
          wasConnected.current = value;
        },
        onStopped,
      ),
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
    [],
  );

  const ask = useCallback(
    (question: string) => {
      const q = question.trim();
      if (!q || s.job) return;
      api.ask(mapId, q, s.selection).then(() => setDraft(''), (e: Error) => dispatch({ type: 'error', message: e.message }));
    },
    [mapId, s.job, s.selection],
  );

  const onFix = (fixId: string, action: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'undo') => {
    if (action === 'approve') dispatch({ type: 'fixStatus', fixId, status: 'applying', problems: [] });
    api[action](mapId, fixId).catch((e: ApiError) => {
      if (action === 'approve') dispatch({ type: 'fixStatus', fixId, status: 'failed', problems: e.problems.length ? e.problems : [e.message] });
      else dispatch({ type: 'error', message: [e.message, ...e.problems].join(' ') });
    });
  };

  // A question about a different part of the app: make a new map for it (and go there), or answer it in words here.
  const onOffer = (answerId: string, choice: 'map' | 'words') => {
    api.offer(mapId, answerId, choice).then(
      (r) => { if (r.id) navigate(pageUrl(r.id)); },
      (e: Error) => dispatch({ type: 'error', message: e.message }),
    );
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      const typing = e.target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement || e.target instanceof HTMLInputElement;
      // Esc steps back one level at a time: walkthrough, then selection, then the answer, to the whole map.
      if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        if (s.tour !== null) dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: null });
        else if (selSize(s.selection)) dispatch({ type: 'clearSelection' });
        else dispatch({ type: 'overview' });
        return;
      }
      if (typing || s.tour === null) return;
      if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour + 1 });
      if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour - 1 });
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey);
  }, [s.tour, s.selection]);

  const shown = s.answers.find((a) => a.id === s.shown);
  const pendingFix = shown?.fix && ['proposed', 'applying', 'failed'].includes(s.fixes[shown.fix.id]?.status ?? '') ? shown.fix : null;
  const onSelect = useCallback((kind: keyof Sel, id: string, additive: boolean) => dispatch({ type: 'select', kind, id, additive }), []);
  const onClear = useCallback(() => dispatch({ type: 'clearSelection' }), []);
  const drawn = visibleMap(s);
  const added = addedIds(s);

  return (
    // The provider wraps the whole screen so the zoom buttons in the top bar can reach the map.
    <ReactFlowProvider>
    <div className="app">
      <header className="topbar">
        <a className="brand" href={pageUrl()}>illuminate</a>
        {s.meta?.parent && <a className="crumb" href={pageUrl(s.meta.parent.mapId)} title={`Back to the map this one came from: ${s.meta.parent.question}`}>← {s.meta.parent.question}</a>}
        <MapSwitcher mapId={mapId} question={s.map?.question ?? s.job?.question ?? ''} />
        <a className="tool new-map" href={pageUrl()} title="Ask a new question and make a map for it">＋ New map</a>
        <Summary report={s.report} />
        <span className="grow" />
        {s.map && <ZoomButtons />}
        {s.map && s.map.tour.length > 0 && <button className="tool" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour === null ? 0 : null })}>{s.tour === null ? 'Walkthrough' : 'Leave walkthrough'}</button>}
        <StopButton busy={!!s.job} onStopped={onStopped} onError={(message) => dispatch({ type: 'error', message })} />
        <span className={s.connected ? 'live on' : 'live'} title={s.connected ? 'Connected to illuminate' : 'Reconnecting to illuminate…'} />
      </header>
      <div className="body">
        <div className="canvas">
          {s.map && drawn ? (
            <>
              <MapGraph map={drawn} report={s.report} selection={s.selection} view={currentView(s)} fresh={s.fresh} added={added} ghost={pendingFix ?? null} onSelect={onSelect} onClear={onClear} />
              <Composer
                map={s.map}
                selection={s.selection}
                draft={draft}
                busy={!!s.job}
                onDraft={setDraft}
                onRemove={(kind, id) => dispatch({ type: 'select', kind, id, additive: true })}
                onSend={() => ask(draft)}
              />
            </>
          ) : (
            <div className="empty">{s.phase === 'making' ? <div className="pulse">Claude is exploring the code…</div> : null}</div>
          )}
        </div>
        <Panel state={s} dispatch={dispatch} onDraft={setDraft} onFix={onFix} onFocus={(id) => dispatch({ type: 'focus', id })} onOffer={onOffer} />
      </div>
    </div>
    </ReactFlowProvider>
  );
}
// The input bar floating over the map. What's selected rides along as chips; Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { nameOf } from './panel';
import type { Sel } from './state';
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

export type ComposerProps = {
  map: CodeMap;
  selection: Sel;
  draft: string;
  busy: boolean;
  onDraft: (text: string) => void;
  onRemove: (kind: keyof Sel, id: string) => void;
  onSend: () => void;
};

export function Composer({ map, selection, draft, busy, onDraft, onRemove, onSend }: ComposerProps) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null);
  const chips = (['nodes', 'edges', 'absences'] as const).flatMap((kind) => selection[kind].map((id) => ({ kind, id })));

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current;
    if (!el) return;
    el.style.height = 'auto';
    el.style.height = `${Math.min(el.scrollHeight, 140)}px`;
  }, [draft]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (draft) ref.current?.focus();
  }, [draft === '']);

  return (
    <form
      className="composer"
      onSubmit={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        if (!busy && draft.trim()) onSend();
      }}
    >
      {chips.map((c) => (
        <span key={`${c.kind}:${c.id}`} className={`sel-chip sel-${c.kind}`}>
          <span className="sel-text" title={nameOf(map, c.id)}>
            {c.kind === 'absences' ? '✕ ' : '◉ '}
            {nameOf(map, c.id)}
          </span>
          <button type="button" aria-label={`Remove ${nameOf(map, c.id)}`} onClick={() => onRemove(c.kind, c.id)}>×</button>
        </span>
      ))}
      <textarea
        ref={ref}
        id="ask"
        rows={1}
        value={draft}
        placeholder={busy ? 'Claude is working…' : chips.length ? 'Ask about what you selected…' : 'Ask about this map…'}
        onChange={(e) => onDraft(e.target.value)}
        onKeyDown={(e) => {
          if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) {
            e.preventDefault();
            if (!busy && draft.trim()) onSend();
          }
        }}
        aria-label="Ask a question about the map"
      />
      <button type="submit" className="send" disabled={busy || !draft.trim()} aria-label="Send">↑</button>
    </form>
  );
}

```text
// The map itself: areas as containers, steps as boxes, labeled arrows, missing connections as red dashed arrows and a
// proposed fix as a green dashed one. Click to select (shift-click adds).
import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import {
  Background,
  BaseEdge,
  Controls,
  EdgeLabelRenderer,
  Handle,
  MarkerType,
  Position,
  ReactFlow,
  getBezierPath,
  useReactFlow,
  type Edge,
  type EdgeProps,
  type Node,
  type NodeProps,
} from '@xyflow/react';
import { layoutKey, layoutMap, sides, type ExtraEdge, type Layout } from './layout';
import type { Sel, View } from './state';
import type { CheckReport, CodeMap, FixProposal } from './types';

const cls = (...xs: (string | false | null | undefined)[]) => xs.filter(Boolean).join(' ');

type StepData = {
  name: string;
  sub: string;
  kind: string;
  confirmed: boolean;
  selected: boolean;
  hl: boolean;
  dim: boolean;
  fresh: boolean;
  onClick: (additive: boolean) => void;
};
type AreaData = { label: string; note: string | null; dim: boolean };
type LinkData = {
  label: string;
  /** Sideways bend in px, so arrows between the same two steps don't hide each other. */
  offset?: number;
  variant: 'edge' | 'absence' | 'ghost';
  confirmed: boolean;
  hl: boolean;
  dim: boolean;
  selected: boolean;
  onClick?: (additive: boolean) => void;
};
type StepNodeT = Node<StepData, 'step'>;
type AreaNodeT = Node<AreaData, 'area'>;
type LinkEdgeT = Edge<LinkData, 'link'>;

const KIND: Record<string, string> = { entry: 'way in', store: 'store', external: 'outside', job: 'job' };

const SIDES = [['t', Position.Top], ['r', Position.Right], ['b', Position.Bottom], ['l', Position.Left]] as const;

/** A source and a target handle on every side, so an arrow can leave and enter by whichever sides face each other. */
function Handles() {
  return (
    <>
      {SIDES.map(([s, pos]) => <Handle key={`s${s}`} id={`s${s}`} type="source" position={pos} className="handle" isConnectable={false} />)}
      {SIDES.map(([s, pos]) => <Handle key={`t${s}`} id={`t${s}`} type="target" position={pos} className="handle" isConnectable={false} />)}
    </>
  );
}

function StepNode({ data }: NodeProps<StepNodeT>) {
  return (
    // `nopan`: pressing on a step must not start a canvas pan, or the pan can swallow the click.
    <div
      className={cls('step', 'nopan', `kind-${data.kind}`, !data.confirmed && 'unconfirmed', data.selected && 'selected', data.hl && 'hl', data.dim && 'dim')}
      onClick={(e) => {
        e.stopPropagation();
        data.onClick(e.shiftKey || e.metaKey);
      }}
    >
      <Handles />
      {KIND[data.kind] && <span className="step-kind">{KIND[data.kind]}</span>}
      <div className="step-name" title={data.name}>{data.name}</div>
      <div className="step-sub">{data.sub}</div>
      {data.fresh ? (
        <span className="badge badge-new">NEW</span>
      ) : !data.confirmed ? (
        <span className="badge badge-q" title="The checker couldn't confirm this against the code">?</span>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}

function AreaNode({ data }: NodeProps<AreaNodeT>) {
  return (
    <div className={cls('area', data.dim && 'dim')}>
      <div className="area-label">
        {data.label}
        {data.note && <span className="area-note"> · {data.note}</span>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

/** A curve bent `offset` px to one side of the straight line, with its label at the bend. */
function bentPath(sx: number, sy: number, tx: number, ty: number, offset: number): [string, number, number] {
  const len = Math.hypot(tx - sx, ty - sy) || 1;
  const nx = -(ty - sy) / len;
  const ny = (tx - sx) / len;
  const cx = (sx + tx) / 2 + nx * offset * 2;
  const cy = (sy + ty) / 2 + ny * offset * 2;
  return [`M ${sx} ${sy} Q ${cx} ${cy} ${tx} ${ty}`, (sx + tx) / 2 + nx * offset, (sy + ty) / 2 + ny * offset];
}

function LinkEdge({ id, sourceX, sourceY, targetX, targetY, sourcePosition, targetPosition, markerEnd, data }: EdgeProps<LinkEdgeT>) {
  const [path, lx, ly] = data?.offset
    ? bentPath(sourceX, sourceY, targetX, targetY, data.offset)
    : getBezierPath({ sourceX, sourceY, sourcePosition, targetX, targetY, targetPosition });
  if (!data) return null;
  return (
    <>
      {data.selected && <path d={path} className="edge-halo" />}
      <BaseEdge id={id} path={path} markerEnd={markerEnd} interactionWidth={18} />
      <EdgeLabelRenderer>
        <div
          className={cls('link-label', `link-${data.variant}`, !data.confirmed && 'unconfirmed', data.hl && 'hl', data.dim && 'dim', data.selected && 'selected', 'nodrag nopan')}
          style={{ transform: `translate(-50%, -50%) translate(${lx}px, ${ly}px)` }}
          onClick={(e) => {
            e.stopPropagation();
            data.onClick?.(e.shiftKey || e.metaKey);
          }}
        >
          {data.label}
          {!data.confirmed && data.variant === 'edge' && <span className="q"> ?</span>}
        </div>
      </EdgeLabelRenderer>
    </>
  );
}

const nodeTypes = { step: StepNode, area: AreaNode };
const edgeTypes = { link: LinkEdge };

export type GraphProps = {
  map: CodeMap;
  report: CheckReport | null;
  selection: Sel;
  view: View | null;
  fresh: string[];
  /** What answers added: laid out around the original map so its boxes don't move. */
  added: readonly string[];
  ghost: FixProposal | null;
  onSelect: (kind: keyof Sel, id: string, additive: boolean) => void;
  onClear: () => void;
};

/** Node ids a view is about: boxes directly, plus the ends of any arrows or gaps it names. */
function nodesOf(map: CodeMap, ids: readonly string[]): string[] {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const id of ids) {
    if (map.nodes.some((n) => n.id === id)) out.add(id);
    const e = map.edges.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (e) out.add(e.from).add(e.to);
    const a = map.absences.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (a?.between) out.add(a.between.from).add(a.between.to);
  }
  return [...out];
}

const shortClaim = (claim: string) => (claim.length > 28 ? `${claim.slice(0, 26)}…` : claim);

export function MapGraph(p: GraphProps) {
  // A proposed fix's arrow is drawn only while both of its ends are (a hidden layer can hide one).
  const ghost = p.ghost?.connects && p.map.nodes.some((n) => n.id === p.ghost!.connects!.from) && p.map.nodes.some((n) => n.id === p.ghost!.connects!.to) ? p.ghost : null;
  const extra: ExtraEdge[] = useMemo(() => (ghost?.connects ? [{ id: ghost.id, from: ghost.connects.from, to: ghost.connects.to }] : []), [ghost]);
  const key = layoutKey(p.map, extra, p.added);
  const [layout, setLayout] = useState<{ key: string; layout: Layout } | null>(null);
  const rf = useReactFlow();

  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    void layoutMap(p.map, extra, new Set(p.added)).then((l) => live && setLayout({ key, layout: l }));
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
    // The key captures everything the layout depends on.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [key]);

  const hl = p.view?.highlight.length ? new Set(p.view.highlight) : null;
  const lit = useMemo(() => (hl ? new Set(nodesOf(p.map, [...hl])) : null), [hl, p.map]);
  const sel = p.selection;

  const nodes = useMemo((): (StepNodeT | AreaNodeT)[] => {
    if (!layout) return [];
    const l = layout.layout;
    const reached = (areaId: string) => !lit || p.map.nodes.some((n) => n.area === areaId && lit.has(n.id));
    const areaNodes: AreaNodeT[] = p.map.areas.flatMap((a) => {
      const box = l.areas[a.id];
      if (!box) return [];
      return [{
        id: `area:${a.id}`,
        type: 'area' as const,
        position: { x: box.x, y: box.y },
        style: { width: box.w, height: box.h },
        data: { label: a.label, note: null, dim: !reached(a.id) },
        selectable: false,
        draggable: false,
        zIndex: 0,
      }];
    });
    const stepNodes: StepNodeT[] = p.map.nodes.flatMap((n) => {
      const box = l.nodes[n.id];
      if (!box) return [];
      const sub = n.symbol ? n.symbol.slice(n.symbol.indexOf('#') + 1) : `${n.evidence[0]!.file.split('/').pop()}:${n.evidence[0]!.line}`;
      return [{
        id: n.id,
        type: 'step' as const,
        parentId: `area:${n.area}`,
        extent: 'parent' as const,
        position: { x: box.x, y: box.y },
        data: {
          name: n.name,
          sub,
          kind: n.kind,
          confirmed: p.report?.nodes[n.id]?.status === 'confirmed',
          selected: sel.nodes.includes(n.id),
          hl: !!lit?.has(n.id),
          dim: !!lit && !lit.has(n.id),
          fresh: p.fresh.includes(n.id),
          onClick: (additive) => p.onSelect('nodes', n.id, additive),
        },
        draggable: false,
        zIndex: 1,
      }];
    });
    return [...areaNodes, ...stepNodes];
  }, [layout, p.map, p.report, sel, lit, p.fresh, p.onSelect]);

  const edges = useMemo((): LinkEdgeT[] => {
    if (!layout) return [];
    const marker = (color: string) => ({ type: MarkerType.ArrowClosed, width: 16, height: 16, color });
    const on = (id: string) => !!hl?.has(id);
    const handles = (from: string, to: string) => {
      const [a, b] = sides(p.map, layout.layout, from, to);
      return { sourceHandle: `s${a}`, targetHandle: `t${b}` };
    };
    const out: LinkEdgeT[] = p.map.edges.map((e) => {
      const confirmed = p.report?.edges[e.id]?.status === 'confirmed';
      const isHl = on(e.id) || (!!lit && lit.has(e.from) && lit.has(e.to) && !hl);
      const variant = 'edge' as const;
      return {
        id: `e:${e.id}`,
        source: e.from,
        target: e.to,
        ...handles(e.from, e.to),
        type: 'link' as const,
        className: cls('link', `link-${variant}`, !confirmed && 'unconfirmed', on(e.id) && 'hl', !!hl && !on(e.id) && 'dim', sel.edges.includes(e.id) && 'selected'),
        markerEnd: marker(on(e.id) ? 'var(--accent)' : 'var(--line-strong)'),
        zIndex: 2,
        data: {
          label: e.label,
          variant,
          confirmed,
          hl: isHl,
          dim: !!hl && !on(e.id),
          selected: sel.edges.includes(e.id),
          onClick: (additive) => p.onSelect('edges', e.id, additive),
        },
      };
    });
    const fixes = (a: { from: string; to: string }) => ghost?.connects?.from === a.from && ghost.connects.to === a.to;
    for (const a of p.map.absences) {
      if (!a.between) continue;
      // While a fix for this gap is proposed, its green arrow takes the gap's place.
      if (fixes(a.between)) continue;
      const confirmed = p.report?.absences[a.id]?.status === 'confirmed';
      out.push({
        id: `a:${a.id}`,
        source: a.between.from,
        target: a.between.to,
        ...handles(a.between.from, a.between.to),
        type: 'link',
        className: cls('link', 'link-absence', !confirmed && 'unconfirmed', on(a.id) && 'hl', !!hl && !on(a.id) && 'dim', sel.absences.includes(a.id) && 'selected'),
        markerEnd: marker('var(--dead)'),
        zIndex: 2,
        data: {
          label: `✕ ${shortClaim(a.claim)}`,
          variant: 'absence',
          confirmed,
          hl: on(a.id),
          dim: !!hl && !on(a.id),
          selected: sel.absences.includes(a.id),
          onClick: (additive) => p.onSelect('absences', a.id, additive),
        },
      });
    }
    if (ghost?.connects) {
      out.push({
        id: `g:${ghost.id}`,
        source: ghost.connects.from,
        target: ghost.connects.to,
        ...handles(ghost.connects.from, ghost.connects.to),
        type: 'link',
        className: 'link link-ghost',
        markerEnd: marker('var(--ok)'),
        zIndex: 3,
        data: { label: `+ ${ghost.connects.label}`, variant: 'ghost', confirmed: true, hl: true, dim: false, selected: false },
      });
    }
    // Arrows that join the same two steps (either way round) bend apart, so each line and label stays visible.
    const byPair = new Map<string, LinkEdgeT[]>();
    for (const e of out) {
      const key = [e.source, e.target].sort().join('|');
      byPair.set(key, [...(byPair.get(key) ?? []), e]);
    }
    for (const group of byPair.values()) {
      if (group.length < 2) continue;
      group.forEach((e, i) => {
        if (e.data) e.data.offset = (i - (group.length - 1) / 2) * 44;
      });
    }
    return out;
  }, [layout, p.map, p.report, sel, hl, lit, ghost, p.onSelect]);

  // The camera follows the view: fly to what's in focus, or show the whole map. It waits (a frame at a time) until
  // React Flow has measured every box, or it would fit an empty canvas.
  const viewKey = JSON.stringify([layout?.key, p.view?.focus, p.view?.highlight]);
  const firstFit = useRef(true);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!layout) return;
    const ids = p.view ? nodesOf(p.map, p.view.highlight.length ? p.view.highlight : p.view.focus ? [p.view.focus] : []) : [];
    let frame = 0;
    let handle = 0;
    const tick = () => {
      const ns = rf.getNodes();
      // Measurements live on React Flow's internal nodes, not on the (controlled) nodes we pass in.
      if (!ns.length || !ns.every((n) => rf.getInternalNode(n.id)?.measured?.width)) {
        if (frame++ < 60) handle = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
        return;
      }
      const duration = firstFit.current ? 0 : 650;
      firstFit.current = false;
      // Keep clear of the input bar along the bottom and the zoom controls on the right.
      const padding = ids.length
        ? ({ top: '60px', left: '60px', right: '80px', bottom: '130px' } as const)
        : ({ top: '28px', left: '28px', right: '64px', bottom: '110px' } as const);
      void rf.fitView(ids.length ? { nodes: ids.map((n) => ({ id: n })), duration, padding, maxZoom: 1.15 } : { duration, padding, maxZoom: 1.1 });
    };
    handle = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(handle);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [viewKey]);


  return (
    <ReactFlow
      nodes={nodes}
      edges={edges}
      nodeTypes={nodeTypes}
      edgeTypes={edgeTypes}
      // Steps select themselves (see StepNode); this handler only keeps React Flow from turning their pointer events off.
      onNodeClick={() => undefined}
      onEdgeClick={(e, edge) => {
        if (edge.id.startsWith('e:')) p.onSelect('edges', edge.id.slice(2), e.shiftKey || e.metaKey);
        if (edge.id.startsWith('a:')) p.onSelect('absences', edge.id.slice(2), e.shiftKey || e.metaKey);
      }}
      onPaneClick={p.onClear}
      panOnDrag
      elementsSelectable={false}
      nodesDraggable={false}
      nodesConnectable={false}
      minZoom={0.15}
      maxZoom={2}
    >
      <Background gap={24} size={1} />
      <Controls showInteractive={false} position="bottom-right" />
    </ReactFlow>
  );
}

```text
// The side panel: what the map is, the walkthrough, answers at three depths with their sources, fixes to approve,
// details of whatever is selected, and live progress while Claude works.
import type { Dispatch, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { pageUrl } from './api';
import { layersOf, type Action, type Depth, type FixState, type State } from './state';
import type { Answer, CheckReport, ClaimCheck, CodeMap } from './types';

const cls = (...xs: (string | false | null | undefined)[]) => xs.filter(Boolean).join(' ');

/** A readable name for any id on the map. */
export function nameOf(map: CodeMap, id: string): string {
  const n = map.nodes.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (n) return n.name;
  const e = map.edges.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (e) return `${nameOf(map, e.from)} → ${nameOf(map, e.to)}`;
  const a = map.absences.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (a) return a.claim;
  const area = map.areas.find((x) => x.id === id);
  return area?.label ?? id;
}

function checkOf(report: CheckReport | null, id: string): ClaimCheck | { status: 'confirmed' | 'unconfirmed'; reasons: string[]; evidence?: never } | null {
  if (!report) return null;
  return report.nodes[id] ?? report.edges[id] ?? (report.absences[id] ? { status: report.absences[id]!.status, reasons: report.absences[id]!.reasons } : null);
}

function Card({ eyebrow, title, children, tone, onClose }: { eyebrow?: string; title?: ReactNode; children: ReactNode; tone?: 'ai' | 'ok' | 'dead'; onClose?: () => void }) {
  return (
    <section className={cls('card', tone && `card-${tone}`)}>
      {onClose && <button className="card-close" aria-label="Close" title="Back to the whole map (Esc)" onClick={onClose}>×</button>}
      {eyebrow && <div className="eyebrow">{eyebrow}</div>}
      {title && <h2 className="card-title">{title}</h2>}
      {children}
    </section>
  );
}

function Depths({ depth, dispatch, texts }: { depth: Depth; dispatch: Dispatch<Action>; texts: Partial<Record<Depth, string>> }) {
  const tabs: [Depth, string][] = [['concept', 'Concept'], ['how', 'How it works'], ['code', 'Code']];
  const available = tabs.filter(([d]) => texts[d]);
  const shown = texts[depth] ? depth : (available[0]?.[0] ?? 'concept');
  if (!available.length) return null;
  return (
    <div className="depths">
      <div className="tabs" role="tablist">
        {available.map(([d, label]) => (
          <button key={d} role="tab" aria-selected={shown === d} className={cls('tab', shown === d && 'on')} onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'depth', depth: d })}>
            {label}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className={cls('depth-text', shown === 'code' && 'mono')}>{texts[shown]}</div>
    </div>
  );
}

function Chips({ map, report, ids, onPick }: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport | null; ids: { id: string; status: string }[]; onPick: (id: string) => void }) {
  if (!ids.length) return null;
  return (
    <div className="chips">
      {ids.map(({ id, status }) => (
        <button key={id} className={cls('chip', status !== 'confirmed' && 'chip-unconfirmed')} onClick={() => onPick(id)} title={status === 'confirmed' ? 'Confirmed against the code' : "Couldn't confirm against the code"}>
          <span className={status === 'confirmed' ? 'tick' : 'qmark'}>{status === 'confirmed' ? '✓' : '?'}</span>
          {nameOf(map, id)}
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

function Progress({ lines, working }: { lines: string[]; working: boolean }) {
  const shown = lines.slice(-8);
  return (
    <ul className="progress">
      {shown.map((l, i) => (
        <li key={`${i}-${l}`} className={cls(working && i === shown.length - 1 && 'running')}>
          <span className="ic">{working && i === shown.length - 1 ? '…' : '✓'}</span>
          {l}
        </li>
      ))}
      {!shown.length && working && <li className="running"><span className="ic">…</span>Starting</li>}
    </ul>
  );
}

function FixCard({ fix, onApprove, onReject, onUndo, map }: { fix: FixState; map: CodeMap; onApprove: () => void; onReject: () => void; onUndo: () => void }) {
  const p = fix.proposal;
  const dirty = p.files.filter((f) => f.uncommitted);
  if (fix.status === 'applied') {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow="Fix applied · re-checked" tone="ok">
        <ul className="progress">
          <li><span className="ic">✓</span>Changed {p.files.length} {p.files.length === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'}: {p.files.map((f) => f.file).join(', ')}</li>
          {fix.edgeId && <li><span className="ic">✓</span>New confirmed connection: {nameOf(map, fix.edgeId)}</li>}
          {fix.closed.length > 0 && <li><span className="ic">✓</span>Closed: {fix.closed.length === 1 ? 'the missing connection' : `${fix.closed.length} missing connections`}</li>}
        </ul>
        {fix.undoable
          ? <div className="btns"><button className="btn" onClick={onUndo}>Undo this fix</button></div>
          : <p className="muted small">Undo ended when illuminate stopped. Use git to reverse it.</p>}
      </Card>
    );
  }
  if (fix.status === 'rejected' || fix.status === 'undone') {
    return <Card eyebrow={fix.status === 'undone' ? 'Fix undone' : 'Fix rejected'}><p className="muted">{p.summary}</p>{fix.status === 'undone' && <div className="btns"><button className="btn" onClick={onApprove}>Apply it again</button></div>}</Card>;
  }
  return (
    <Card eyebrow={`Proposed fix · ${p.files.length} ${p.files.length === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'} · nothing changed yet`} tone="ai">
      <p>{p.summary}</p>
      {p.connects && <p className="muted small">The green dashed arrow is the connection it adds.</p>}
      <pre className="diff">{p.diff.split('\n').map((l, i) => <span key={i} className={l.startsWith('+ ') ? 'add' : l.startsWith('- ') ? 'del' : l.includes(' · ') ? 'file' : ''}>{l}{'\n'}</span>)}</pre>
      {dirty.length > 0 ? (
        <p className="warn small">⚠ {dirty.map((f) => f.file).join(', ')} {dirty.length === 1 ? 'has' : 'have'} uncommitted changes. They'll be kept; the fix applies on top.</p>
      ) : null}
      {fix.problems.length > 0 && <ul className="problems">{fix.problems.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ul>}
      <div className="btns">
        <button className="btn primary" disabled={fix.status === 'applying'} onClick={onApprove}>{fix.status === 'applying' ? 'Applying…' : 'Approve'}</button>
        <button className="btn" onClick={onReject}>Reject</button>
      </div>
      <p className="muted small">Won't apply if these files change first.</p>
    </Card>
  );
}

export type PanelProps = {
  state: State;
  dispatch: Dispatch<Action>;
  onDraft: (text: string) => void;
  onFix: (fixId: string, action: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'undo') => void;
  onFocus: (id: string) => void;
  onOffer: (answerId: string, choice: 'map' | 'words') => void;
};

export function Panel({ state: s, dispatch, onDraft, onFix, onFocus, onOffer }: PanelProps) {
  const map = s.map;
  const job = s.job;

  if (s.phase === 'loading') return <aside className="panel"><Card><p className="muted">Loading…</p></Card></aside>;
  if (s.phase === 'missing') return <aside className="panel"><Card title="No map here"><p className="muted">This map isn't in this repo.</p></Card></aside>;
  if (!map) {
    return (
      <aside className="panel">
        {job && (
          <Card eyebrow="Making your map" title={job.question} tone="ai">
            <Progress lines={job.progress} working />
          </Card>
        )}
        {s.phase === 'failed' && <Card title="The map couldn't be made" tone="dead"><p>{s.error}</p></Card>}
      </aside>
    );
  }

  const answer = s.answers.find((a) => a.id === s.shown) ?? null;
  const fix = answer?.fix ? s.fixes[answer.fix.id] ?? null : null;
  const stop = s.tour !== null ? map.tour[s.tour] : null;
  const selected = [...s.selection.nodes, ...s.selection.edges, ...s.selection.absences];

  return (
    <aside className="panel">
      {s.error && <div className="banner banner-dead" role="alert">{s.error}<button className="link-btn" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'error', message: null })}>Dismiss</button></div>}

      {job?.kind === 'ask' && (
        <Card eyebrow="Claude is working" title={`“${job.question}”`} tone="ai">
          <Progress lines={job.progress} working />
        </Card>
      )}

      {stop && s.tour !== null && (
        <Card eyebrow={`Walkthrough · stop ${s.tour + 1} of ${map.tour.length}`} title={stop.title}>
          <div className="dots" aria-hidden="true">
            {map.tour.map((t, i) => <i key={t.id} className={cls(i === s.tour && 'on', i < s.tour! && 'done')} />)}
          </div>
          <p className="depth-text">{stop.text}</p>
          {stop.terms?.length ? <p className="muted small">Terms: {stop.terms.join(', ')}</p> : null}
          <div className="tour-nav">
            <button className="btn" disabled={s.tour === 0} onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour! - 1 })}>◀ Back</button>
            <button className="btn" onClick={() => onDraft(`About “${stop.title}”: `)}>Ask about this step</button>
            <span className="grow" />
            {s.tour < map.tour.length - 1
              ? <button className="btn primary" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour! + 1 })}>Next ▶</button>
              : <button className="btn primary" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: null })}>Done</button>}
          </div>
          <div className="kbd">← → to step · Esc to leave</div>
        </Card>
      )}

      {!stop && answer?.offer && <OfferCard answer={answer} busy={!!job} onOffer={onOffer} onClose={() => dispatch({ type: 'overview' })} />}

      {!stop && answer && !answer.offer && (
        <Card
          eyebrow={`Answer · ${answer.source === 'map' ? 'from the map' : 'looked in the code'}${answer.added.length ? ` · added ${answer.added.length} to the map` : ''}`}
          title={`“${answer.question}”`}
          onClose={() => dispatch({ type: 'overview' })}
        >
          <Depths depth={s.depth} dispatch={dispatch} texts={{ concept: answer.concept, how: answer.how, code: answer.code }} />
          {(() => {
            // Sources as the map is now: drop what a later fix removed, and show each one's current status.
            const refs = answer.refs.filter((r) => r.status !== 'unknown' && checkOf(s.report, r.id)).map((r) => ({ id: r.id, status: checkOf(s.report, r.id)!.status }));
            return refs.length > 0 && <div className="basis"><div className="eyebrow">Based on</div><Chips map={map} report={s.report} ids={refs} onPick={onFocus} /></div>;
          })()}
          {answer.problems.filter((x) => !x.startsWith('The proposed fix')).length > 0 && (
            <details className="problems-box"><summary>{answer.problems.length} thing{answer.problems.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} Claude found but couldn't confirm</summary><ul className="problems">{answer.problems.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ul></details>
          )}
        </Card>
      )}

      {!stop && fix && <FixCard fix={fix} map={map} onApprove={() => onFix(fix.proposal.id, 'approve')} onReject={() => onFix(fix.proposal.id, 'reject')} onUndo={() => onFix(fix.proposal.id, 'undo')} />}
      {!stop && answer?.problems.some((x) => x.startsWith('The proposed fix')) && (
        <Card eyebrow="The proposed fix can't be applied" tone="dead"><ul className="problems">{answer.problems.filter((x) => x.startsWith('The proposed fix')).map((x) => <li key={x}>{x.replace('The proposed fix can\'t be applied: ', '')}</li>)}</ul><p className="muted small">Ask again, or ask for a smaller change.</p></Card>
      )}

      {!stop && selected.length > 0 && <Selected map={map} report={s.report} ids={selected} depth={s.depth} dispatch={dispatch} />}

      {!stop && !answer && !selected.length && !job && (
        <Card eyebrow="This map" title={map.question}>
          {map.tour.length > 0 && <div className="btns"><button className="btn primary" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: 0 })}>Take the walkthrough ({map.tour.length} stops)</button></div>}
          <p className="muted small">Click a box or arrow to ask about it. Shift-click for several.</p>
        </Card>
      )}

      {!stop && <Layers state={s} dispatch={dispatch} />}

      {s.answers.length > (answer ? 1 : 0) && !stop && (
        <Card eyebrow={answer ? 'Earlier questions' : 'Questions on this map'}>
          <ul className="history">
            {s.answers.slice().reverse().map((a) => (
              <li key={a.id}><button className={cls('link-btn', a.id === s.shown && 'on')} onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'show', answerId: a.id })}>{a.question}</button></li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </Card>
      )}
    </aside>
  );
}

/** "This looks like a different part of the app": a new map for it (or the one that already covers it), or words. */
function OfferCard({ answer, busy, onOffer, onClose }: { answer: Answer; busy: boolean; onOffer: (answerId: string, choice: 'map' | 'words') => void; onClose: () => void }) {
  const o = answer.offer!;
  if (o.status === 'mapped') {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow="A different part of the app" title={`“${answer.question}”`} onClose={onClose}>
        <p className="muted">You made a new map for this.</p>
        {o.mapId && <div className="btns"><a className="btn primary" href={pageUrl(o.mapId)}>Open it</a></div>}
      </Card>
    );
  }
  if (o.status === 'answered') {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow="A different part of the app" title={`“${answer.question}”`} onClose={onClose}>
        <p className="muted">Answered in words, below.</p>
      </Card>
    );
  }
  return (
    <Card eyebrow="A different part of the app" title={`“${answer.question}”`} tone="ai" onClose={onClose}>
      {o.existing && <p>There's already a map for it: “{o.existing.question}”.</p>}
      <div className="btns">
        {o.existing && <a className="btn primary" href={pageUrl(o.existing.id)}>Open that map</a>}
        <button className={o.existing ? 'btn' : 'btn primary'} onClick={() => onOffer(answer.id, 'map')}>Make a new map for this</button>
        <button className="btn" disabled={busy} onClick={() => onOffer(answer.id, 'words')} title={busy ? 'Claude is still working on this map' : undefined}>Just answer in words</button>
      </div>
    </Card>
  );
}

/** What answers added, as layers to show or hide. Hiding them all shows the map as it was first drawn. */
function Layers({ state, dispatch }: { state: State; dispatch: Dispatch<Action> }) {
  const layers = layersOf(state);
  if (!layers.length) return null;
  const allHidden = layers.every((l) => !l.visible);
  return (
    <Card eyebrow="Added by your questions">
      <ul className="layers">
        {layers.map((l) => (
          <li key={l.answerId}>
            <label>
              <input type="checkbox" checked={l.visible} onChange={(e) => dispatch({ type: 'layer', answerId: l.answerId, visible: e.target.checked })} />
              <span className="layer-n">+{l.ids.length}</span>
              <span className="layer-q">{l.question}</span>
            </label>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <div className="btns">
        <button className="btn" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'allLayers', visible: allHidden })}>{allHidden ? 'Show everything' : 'Show the original map'}</button>
      </div>
    </Card>
  );
}

function Selected({ map, report, ids, depth, dispatch }: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport | null; ids: string[]; depth: Depth; dispatch: Dispatch<Action> }) {
  if (ids.length > 1) {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow={`${ids.length} selected`}>
        <Chips map={map} report={report} ids={ids.map((id) => ({ id, status: checkOf(report, id)?.status ?? 'unknown' }))} onPick={() => undefined} />
      </Card>
    );
  }
  const id = ids[0]!;
  const node = map.nodes.find((n) => n.id === id);
  const edge = map.edges.find((e) => e.id === id);
  const gap = map.absences.find((a) => a.id === id);
  const c = checkOf(report, id);
  const evidence = node?.evidence ?? edge?.evidence ?? [];
  const evidenceChecks = c && 'evidence' in c && c.evidence ? c.evidence : [];
  return (
    <Card eyebrow={node ? 'Step' : edge ? 'Connection' : 'Missing connection'} title={nameOf(map, id)} tone={gap ? 'dead' : undefined}>
      {node?.explain && <Depths depth={depth} dispatch={dispatch} texts={node.explain} />}
      {gap && <p>Nothing in the code connects these. Searching <code>{gap.search.pattern}</code>{gap.search.paths ? <> in <code>{gap.search.paths.join(', ')}</code></> : null}: {report?.absences[gap.id]?.found ?? '?'} {report?.absences[gap.id]?.found === 1 ? 'match' : 'matches'}.</p>}
      {c && c.status !== 'confirmed' && <div className="warn small">Couldn't confirm against the code: {c.reasons.join('; ')}</div>}
      {evidence.length > 0 && (
        <div className="basis">
          <div className="eyebrow">In the code</div>
          <div className="chips">
            {evidence.map((e, i) => {
              const ok = evidenceChecks[i]?.ok ?? false;
              return <span key={i} className={cls('chip static', !ok && 'chip-unconfirmed')}><span className={ok ? 'tick' : 'qmark'}>{ok ? '✓' : '?'}</span>{e.file}:{evidenceChecks[i]?.foundAt ?? e.line}</span>;
            })}
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </Card>
  );
}
// The start page: maps already made in this repo, and a box to ask a new question.
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { api, connect, pageUrl } from './api';
import { navigate } from './nav';
import { StopButton } from './stop';
import type { MapMeta } from './types';

export function Home({ onStopped }: { onStopped: () => void }) {
  const [repo, setRepo] = useState('');
  const [maps, setMaps] = useState<MapMeta[] | null>(null);
  const [making, setMaking] = useState<{ id: string; question: string }[]>([]);
  const [question, setQuestion] = useState('');
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);

  // Stay connected while this page is open: it keeps illuminate running, and hears when it stops.
  useEffect(() => connect(() => {}, () => {}, onStopped), [onStopped]);
  useEffect(() => {
    api.list().then((r) => { setRepo(r.repo); setMaps(r.maps); setMaking(r.making); }, (e: Error) => setError(e.message));
  }, []);

  const submit = async () => {
    if (!question.trim()) return;
    setBusy(true);
    try {
      const { id } = await api.make(question.trim());
      navigate(pageUrl(id));
    } catch (e) {
      setError((e as Error).message);
      setBusy(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <main className="home">
      <div className="eyebrow">illuminate{repo ? ` · ${repo}` : ''}</div>
      <h1>Ask how your code works</h1>
      <p className="muted lede">Every box and arrow is checked against the code.</p>
      <form className="home-ask" onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); void submit(); }}>
        <input id="question" value={question} onChange={(e) => setQuestion(e.target.value)} placeholder="What happens when a user signs up?" aria-label="Your question" autoFocus />
        <button className="btn primary" disabled={busy || !question.trim()}>{busy ? 'Starting…' : 'Map it'}</button>
      </form>
      {error && <div className="banner banner-dead" role="alert">{error}</div>}
      {making.length > 0 && (
        <section>
          <h2 className="section-title">Being made now</h2>
          <ul className="maplist">{making.map((m) => <li key={m.id}><a href={pageUrl(m.id)}>{m.question}</a><span className="muted small">Claude is exploring…</span></li>)}</ul>
        </section>
      )}
      <section>
        <h2 className="section-title">Maps in this repo</h2>
        {maps === null ? <p className="muted">Loading…</p> : maps.length === 0 ? <p className="muted">None yet.</p> : (
          <ul className="maplist">
            {maps.map((m) => (
              <li key={m.id}>
                <a href={pageUrl(m.id)}>{m.question}</a>
                <span className="muted small">{new Date(m.updatedAt).toLocaleString()}{m.commit ? ` · ${m.commit.slice(0, 7)}` : ''}</span>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        )}
      </section>
      <footer className="home-foot">
        <StopButton busy={making.length > 0} onStopped={onStopped} onError={setError} />
      </footer>
    </main>
  );
}
// Stopping illuminate from the page, and what a tab shows once it has stopped (by the button, Ctrl+C, or on its own).
import { api } from './api';

export function StopButton({ busy, onStopped, onError }: { busy: boolean; onStopped: () => void; onError: (message: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <button
      className="tool"
      disabled={busy}
      title={busy ? 'Claude is still working' : 'Maps stay saved. Undo for applied fixes ends.'}
      onClick={() => api.stop().then(onStopped, (e: Error) => onError(e.message))}
    >
      Stop illuminate
    </button>
  );
}

export function Stopped() {
  return (
    <main className="home">
      <h1>illuminate has stopped</h1>
      <p className="muted lede">
        Maps are saved in <code>.illuminate/maps</code>. Run <code>illume open</code> in the repo to see them again.
      </p>
    </main>
  );
}
