```text
// Laying the map out with ELK, in two passes: each area's steps stack top to bottom in the order the arrows go, then
// the areas themselves run left to right along the arrows that cross between them. Missing connections and proposed
// fixes take part like arrows do. Arrows attach to the sides of the boxes that face each other.
// What answers added is laid out around the map as it was first drawn, so the boxes someone already knows never move:
// additions to an existing area go in rows below its steps, new areas go to the right.
import type { ElkExtendedEdge, ElkNode } from 'elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js';
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

export const NODE_W = 210;
export const NODE_H = 66;
export type Box = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };
/** Area boxes are absolute; node boxes are relative to their area. */
export type Layout = { areas: Record<string, Box>; nodes: Record<string, Box>; width: number; height: number };
export type ExtraEdge = { id: string; from: string; to: string };
export type Side = 't' | 'r' | 'b' | 'l';

// ELK is most of the bundle; load it on first layout so the page shell shows up first.
let elk: Promise<{ layout(graph: ElkNode): Promise<ElkNode> }> | null = null;
const getElk = () => (elk ??= import('elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js').then((m) => new m.default()));

const LAYERED = {
  'elk.algorithm': 'layered',
  'elk.layered.nodePlacement.strategy': 'NETWORK_SIMPLEX',
  'elk.layered.considerModelOrder.strategy': 'NODES_AND_EDGES',
};

/** Every connection on the map, as from → to pairs between boxes. */
function links(map: CodeMap, extra: readonly ExtraEdge[]): { id: string; from: string; to: string }[] {
  const ids = new Set(map.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
  return [
    ...map.edges.map((e) => ({ id: `e:${e.id}`, from: e.from, to: e.to })),
    ...map.absences.flatMap((a) => (a.between ? [{ id: `a:${a.id}`, from: a.between.from, to: a.between.to }] : [])),
    ...extra.map((x) => ({ id: `x:${x.id}`, from: x.from, to: x.to })),
  ].filter((l) => ids.has(l.from) && ids.has(l.to) && l.from !== l.to);
}

type Engine = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getElk>>;
const PAD = { top: 46, side: 22, bottom: 22 };
const ROW_GAP = 56;
const COL_GAP = 36;
const AREA_GAP = 48;
const COLUMN_GAP = 120;

/** Pass 1 for one area: its steps top to bottom, with room between rows for arrow labels. */
```

```typescript
// The dock floating along the bottom of the map: the walkthrough, the question box, and zoom. Everything you do to
// the map itself lives here, so the top bar only says which map this is.
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { useReactFlow } from '@xyflow/react';
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

export type DockProps = {
  map: CodeMap;
  /** The walkthrough stop on screen, or null when the walkthrough isn't running. */
  tour: number | null;
  onTour: (stop: number | null) => void;
  /** The question box (the composer). */
  children: ReactNode;
};

export function Dock({ map, tour, onTour, children }: DockProps) {
  const stops = map.tour.length;
  const stop = tour !== null ? map.tour[tour] : undefined;
  return (
    <div className="dock">
      {stops > 0 && (
        <section className="dock-part dock-walk" aria-label="Walkthrough">
          <h2 className="dock-title">Walkthrough</h2>
          {tour === null || !stop ? (
            <button className="dock-start" onClick={() => onTour(0)}>
              Take the walkthrough <span className="muted">{stops} {stops === 1 ? 'stop' : 'stops'}</span>
            </button>
          ) : (
            <div className="dock-row">
              <button className="icon-btn" aria-label="Previous stop" title="Previous stop (←)" disabled={tour === 0} onClick={() => onTour(tour - 1)}>‹</button>
              <span className="walk-now" title={stop.title}>
                <span className="walk-n">{tour + 1} of {stops}</span>
                <span className="walk-title">{stop.title}</span>
              </span>
              {tour < stops - 1
                ? <button className="icon-btn" aria-label="Next stop" title="Next stop (→)" onClick={() => onTour(tour + 1)}>›</button>
                : <button className="icon-btn done" aria-label="Finish the walkthrough" title="Finish the walkthrough" onClick={() => onTour(null)}>✓</button>}
              <button className="icon-btn quiet" aria-label="Leave the walkthrough" title="Leave the walkthrough (Esc)" onClick={() => onTour(null)}>×</button>
            </div>
          )}
        </section>
      )}
      <section className="dock-part dock-ask" aria-label="Ask about the map">
        <h2 className="dock-title">Ask about the map</h2>
        {children}
      </section>
      <ViewTools />
    </div>
  );
}

/** Zoom the map in and out, or fit all of it (the mouse wheel and trackpad zoom too). */
function ViewTools() {
  const rf = useReactFlow();
  return (
    <section className="dock-part" aria-label="View">
      <h2 className="dock-title">View</h2>
      <div className="dock-row">
        <button className="icon-btn" aria-label="Zoom out" title="Zoom out" onClick={() => void rf.zoomOut({ duration: 200 })}>−</button>
        <button className="icon-btn" aria-label="Zoom in" title="Zoom in" onClick={() => void rf.zoomIn({ duration: 200 })}>+</button>
        <button className="icon-btn" aria-label="Fit the whole map" title="Fit the whole map" onClick={() => void rf.fitView({ duration: 300, padding: { top: '32px', left: '32px', right: '32px', bottom: '130px' } })}>⤢</button>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

```

```css
/* illuminate viewer.
   Paper and ink: a cool off-white canvas with dots, white cards outlined in ink, thin arrows labelled in plain text.
   Lamp yellow is the brand and what's lit (the walkthrough and what you selected). Red = gaps, green = confirmed and
   proposed fixes, violet = Claude is working. The card you're focused on is dark, like a note pinned to the map. */
:root {
  --bg: #f3f4f1;
  --paper: #fbfbf9;
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --ink: #1e2421;
  --muted: #69716c;
  --line: #dcdfd8;
  --line-strong: #8b938d;
  --dot: #cdd2c9;
  --path: #1e2421;
  --accent: #0f5c5a;
  --accent-soft: #e2efed;
  --lamp: #f2c230;
  --lamp-soft: #fff6d6;
  --lamp-glow: rgba(242, 194, 48, 0.45);
  --ai: #6b4bb0;
  --ai-soft: #f1ecfa;
  --ok: #2d7a55;
  --ok-soft: #e4f2ea;
  --dead: #cf4a33;
  --dead-soft: #fbe5df;
  --focus-bg: #23292a;
  --focus-ink: #eef1ee;
  --focus-muted: #9da7a2;
  --focus-line: #3b4344;
  --shadow: 0 12px 32px -14px rgba(30, 36, 33, 0.28);
  --font: "Instrument Sans Variable", "Instrument Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  --mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
  color-scheme: light;
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --bg: #151a1b; --paper: #1a1f20; --surface: #1f2526; --ink: #e8ece9; --muted: #9aa39e; --line: #2f3637;
    --line-strong: #6c7571; --dot: #2b3233; --path: #e8ece9; --accent: #5cc2bd; --accent-soft: #17302f;
    --lamp: #f2c230; --lamp-soft: #2f2a15; --lamp-glow: rgba(242, 194, 48, 0.3); --ai: #b49af0; --ai-soft: #262036;
    --ok: #5fd39a; --ok-soft: #13291e; --dead: #ff7a66; --dead-soft: #351c18;
    --focus-bg: #2a3132; --focus-ink: #eef1ee; --focus-muted: #a2aca7; --focus-line: #414a4b;
    --shadow: 0 12px 32px -14px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6); color-scheme: dark;
  }
}

* { box-sizing: border-box; }
html, body, #root { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--ink); font: 400 14px/1.5 var(--font); -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }
button { font: inherit; color: inherit; }
code { font: 500 0.9em var(--mono); }
button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible, select:focus-visible, a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
.muted { color: var(--muted); }
.small { font-size: 12.5px; }
.grow { flex: 1; }
.eyebrow { font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--muted); }

/* ---------- buttons ---------- */
.pill-btn {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink);
  border-radius: 999px; padding: 5px 14px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; flex: none;
}
.pill-btn:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.pill-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }
.btns, .tour-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
.btn { border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); border-radius: 999px; padding: 7px 14px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; }
.btn:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
a.btn { display: inline-block; text-decoration: none; }
.btn.primary { background: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); color: var(--bg); }
.btn.primary:hover { border-color: var(--ink); opacity: 0.88; }
.btn:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }
.icon-btn {
  width: 36px; height: 36px; flex: none; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px;
  background: var(--surface); font-size: 17px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer;
}
.icon-btn:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.icon-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.35; cursor: default; }
.icon-btn.done { background: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); color: var(--bg); font-size: 14px; }
.icon-btn.quiet { border-color: transparent; background: transparent; color: var(--muted); }
.icon-btn.quiet:hover { background: var(--bg); color: var(--ink); }
.link-btn { border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 0; color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer; text-align: left; font-size: 13px; }
.link-btn.on { font-weight: 600; }

/* ---------- layout ---------- */
.app { height: 100%; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr; }
.topbar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; height: 56px; padding: 0 16px; background: var(--paper); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); min-width: 0; }
.brand { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; color: var(--ink); text-decoration: none; letter-spacing: -0.01em; flex: none; }
.brand-mark { width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 7px; background: var(--ink); position: relative; flex: none; }
.brand-mark::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 6.5px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--lamp); box-shadow: 0 0 7px 2px var(--lamp-glow); }
.topbar-map { flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; }
.switcher {
  font: inherit; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14.5px; min-width: 12ch; max-width: 60ch; flex: 0 1 auto; text-overflow: ellipsis;
  border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink); padding: 4px 6px; cursor: pointer;
}
.switcher:hover, .switcher:focus { border-color: var(--line); background: var(--surface); }
.crumb { color: var(--muted); text-decoration: none; font-size: 13px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; flex: 0 1 24ch; min-width: 8ch; }
.crumb:hover { color: var(--accent); }
.summary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 13px; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; flex: none; }
.meter { width: 64px; height: 6px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--dead); overflow: hidden; display: flex; }
.meter b { background: var(--ok); height: 100%; }
.summary.ok .meter { background: var(--ok); }
.live { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--line-strong); flex: none; }
.live.on { background: var(--ok); }
.body { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 400px; min-height: 0; }
@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .body { grid-template-columns: 1fr; grid-template-rows: 64vh auto; }
  .summary { display: none; }
}
.canvas { position: relative; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; background: var(--bg); }
.empty { height: 100%; display: grid; place-items: center; }
.pulse { color: var(--ai); animation: pulse 1.6s ease-in-out infinite; }
@keyframes pulse { 50% { opacity: 0.45; } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .pulse { animation: none; } }

/* ---------- graph ---------- */
.react-flow { --xy-background-color: var(--bg); --xy-background-pattern-color: var(--dot); background: var(--bg); }
.react-flow__attribution { background: transparent; }
.react-flow__node-area, .react-flow__node-step { padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent; }
.area { width: 100%; height: 100%; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 26px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 42%, transparent); transition: opacity 0.25s; }
.area-label { padding: 16px 22px 0; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted); letter-spacing: -0.005em; }
.area-note { font-weight: 400; }
.area.dim { opacity: 0.4; }
.handle { opacity: 0; width: 1px; height: 1px; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; border: 0; }

.step {
  position: relative; width: 232px; height: 96px; padding: 11px 14px 10px; border-radius: 16px; background: var(--surface);
  border: 1.5px solid var(--ink); cursor: pointer; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto; gap: 3px;
  transition: opacity 0.25s, background 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s;
}
.step:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--line); }
.step-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); min-width: 0; }
.step-mark { width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; font-style: normal; font-size: 10.5px; line-height: 1; background: var(--bg); color: var(--muted); flex: none; }
.kind-entry .step-mark { background: var(--ok-soft); color: var(--ok); }
.kind-store .step-mark { background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent); }
.kind-external .step-mark { background: var(--ai-soft); color: var(--ai); }
.kind-job .step-mark { background: var(--lamp-soft); color: #8a6500; }
.step-name { align-self: center; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.25; letter-spacing: -0.01em; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.step-code { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-width: 0; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 999px; padding: 2px 9px; font-size: 11px; }
.step-sub { font: 11px/1.4 var(--mono); color: var(--muted); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; min-width: 0; }
.step.kind-job, .step.kind-external { border-style: dashed; }
.step.unconfirmed { border-style: dashed; border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.step.unconfirmed .step-code { border-style: dashed; }
.step.hl { background: var(--lamp-soft); box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--lamp-glow); }
.step.dim { opacity: 0.32; }
.step.selected { box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px var(--lamp-glow), 0 0 0 1.5px var(--ink); }
.badge-new { margin-left: auto; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--surface); background: var(--ai); border-radius: 999px; padding: 1px 8px; }

.react-flow__edge.link .react-flow__edge-path { stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-width: 1.4; transition: opacity 0.25s; }
.react-flow__edge.link.hl .react-flow__edge-path { stroke: var(--path); stroke-width: 2.2; }
.react-flow__edge.link.unconfirmed .react-flow__edge-path { stroke-dasharray: 4 4; }
/* A gap stays red and a proposed fix stays green even when highlighted. */
.react-flow__edge.link.link-absence .react-flow__edge-path { stroke: var(--dead); stroke-width: 1.8; stroke-dasharray: 6 6; }
.react-flow__edge.link.link-absence.hl .react-flow__edge-path { stroke-width: 2.4; }
.react-flow__edge.link.link-ghost .react-flow__edge-path { stroke: var(--ok); stroke-width: 2.2; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.react-flow__edgelabel-renderer { z-index: 4; }
.react-flow__edge.link.dim { opacity: 0.25; }
.edge-halo { fill: none; stroke: var(--lamp-glow); stroke-width: 14; stroke-linecap: round; }
.link-label {
  position: absolute; pointer-events: all; cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px;
  font-size: 12.5px; color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 72%, var(--bg)); background: var(--bg); border-radius: 8px; padding: 2px 7px;
  white-space: nowrap; transition: opacity 0.25s;
}
.link-label:hover { color: var(--ink); }
.link-label.hl { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }
.link-label.link-absence { color: var(--dead); font-weight: 600; background: transparent; padding: 0; }
.link-label.link-absence .link-text { background: var(--bg); border-radius: 8px; padding: 2px 7px 2px 2px; }
.gap-q {
  width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; flex: none; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--dead); background: var(--dead-soft); border: 1.5px solid var(--dead);
}
.link-label.link-absence.hl .gap-q { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--dead) 22%, transparent); }
.link-label.link-ghost { color: var(--ok); font-weight: 600; border: 1.5px solid var(--ok); background: var(--ok-soft); border-radius: 999px; padding: 2px 10px; cursor: default; }
.link-label.selected { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--lamp-glow); }
.link-label.link-absence.selected { box-shadow: none; }
.link-label.link-absence.selected .gap-q { box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px var(--lamp-glow); }
.link-label.dim { opacity: 0.3; }
.link-label .q { color: var(--muted); }

/* ---------- dock ---------- */
.dock {
  position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: 18px; transform: translateX(-50%); z-index: 5; width: max-content; max-width: calc(100% - 32px);
  display: flex; align-items: stretch; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 18px; box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
.dock-part { display: grid; align-content: start; gap: 6px; padding: 9px 12px 11px; border-left: 1px solid var(--line); min-width: 0; }
.dock-part:first-child { border-left: 0; }
.dock-title { margin: 0; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted); }
.dock-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; }
.dock-start { height: 36px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; background: var(--surface); padding: 0 12px; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; display: inline-flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
.dock-start .muted { font-weight: 400; }
.dock-start:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.walk-now { display: grid; min-width: 0; max-width: 220px; padding: 0 4px; line-height: 1.25; }
.walk-n { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--muted); }
.walk-title { font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.dock-ask { flex: 1 1 360px; }
@media (max-width: 1180px) {
  .dock { flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .dock-ask { order: 3; flex-basis: 100%; border-left: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
}

/* the question box, inside the dock */
.composer { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; gap: 6px; min-width: 300px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; padding: 3px 3px 3px 11px; background: var(--surface); }
.composer:focus-within { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.composer textarea { flex: 1; min-width: 160px; resize: none; border: 0; outline: none; background: transparent; color: var(--ink); font: inherit; font-size: 14px; padding: 5px 0; max-height: 140px; }
.composer textarea:focus-visible { outline: none; }
.sel-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink); background: var(--lamp-soft); border: 1px solid var(--lamp); border-radius: 999px; padding: 2px 4px 2px 9px; margin: 3px 0; }
.sel-text { max-width: 220px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.sel-chip.sel-absences { color: var(--dead); background: var(--dead-soft); border-color: var(--dead); }
.sel-chip button { border: 0; background: transparent; cursor: pointer; padding: 0 4px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; color: inherit; }
.send { width: 30px; height: 30px; flex: none; border-radius: 50%; border: 0; background: var(--lamp); color: #23292a; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; }
.send:disabled { background: var(--bg); color: var(--muted); cursor: default; }

/* ---------- panel ---------- */
.panel { border-left: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--paper); overflow-y: auto; padding: 16px; display: grid; gap: 12px; align-content: start; }
.card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 16px; padding: 15px 17px; display: grid; position: relative; gap: 10px; }
.card-close { position: absolute; top: 10px; right: 10px; width: 26px; height: 26px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--muted); font-size: 18px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; }
.card-close:hover { background: var(--bg); color: var(--ink); }
.card:has(> .card-close) > .eyebrow { padding-right: 28px; }
.card-ai { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ai) 45%, var(--line)); }
.card-ok { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ok) 50%, var(--line)); }
.card-dead { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--dead) 55%, var(--line)); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--dead-soft) 45%, var(--surface)); }
.card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.3; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; text-wrap: balance; }
.card p { margin: 0; }
.tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; }
.tab { border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 4px 11px; cursor: pointer; color: var(--muted); border-radius: 999px; font-size: 12.5px; }
.tab:hover { color: var(--ink); }
.tab.on { color: var(--ink); background: var(--bg); font-weight: 500; }
.depths { display: grid; gap: 9px; }
.depth-text { font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; white-space: pre-wrap; }
.depth-text.mono { font: 12.5px/1.6 var(--mono); }
.chips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
.chip { display: inline-flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; font-size: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); border-radius: 999px; padding: 4px 10px; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; }
.chip:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.chip.static { cursor: default; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 11.5px; }
.chip.static:hover { border-color: var(--line); }
.chip-unconfirmed { border-style: dashed; color: var(--muted); }
.tick { color: var(--ok); font-weight: 700; font-family: var(--font); }
.qmark { color: var(--muted); font-weight: 700; font-family: var(--font); }
.basis { display: grid; gap: 7px; }
.progress { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 5px; font-size: 13px; }
.progress li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 16px 1fr; gap: 6px; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.progress .ic { color: var(--ok); font-weight: 700; }
.progress .running, .progress .running .ic { color: var(--ai); }
.diff { margin: 0; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; font: 11.5px/1.55 var(--mono); overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre; max-height: 260px; }
.diff .add { color: var(--ok); }
.diff .del { color: var(--dead); }
.diff .file { color: var(--muted); font-weight: 600; }
.warn { color: var(--dead); }
.problems { margin: 0; padding-left: 1.1em; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--muted); display: grid; gap: 4px; }
.problems-box summary { cursor: pointer; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--muted); }
.dots { display: flex; gap: 6px; }
.dots i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--line); }
.dots i.done { background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--lamp); }
.dots i.on { background: var(--lamp); width: 22px; border-radius: 4px; }
.kbd { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); }
.history { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 6px; }
.layers { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 7px; }
.layers label { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; cursor: pointer; }
.layers input { accent-color: var(--ink); }
.layer-n { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ai); min-width: 2.5ch; }
.layer-q { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; min-width: 0; }
.banner { border-radius: 12px; padding: 10px 13px; font-size: 13px; display: flex; gap: 10px; justify-content: space-between; align-items: start; }
.banner-dead { background: var(--dead-soft); color: var(--dead); border: 1px solid var(--dead); }

/* The card you're focused on (walkthrough stop, an answer, what you selected): dark, like a note pinned to the map. */
.card-focus { background: var(--focus-bg); border-color: var(--focus-bg); color: var(--focus-ink); box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
.card-focus .eyebrow, .card-focus .muted, .card-focus .kbd, .card-focus .problems, .card-focus .problems-box summary { color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .card-close { color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .card-close:hover { background: var(--focus-line); color: var(--focus-ink); }
.card-focus .tab { color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .tab:hover { color: var(--focus-ink); }
.card-focus .tab.on { background: var(--focus-line); color: #fff; }
.card-focus .chip { background: transparent; border-color: var(--focus-line); color: var(--focus-ink); }
.card-focus .chip:hover { border-color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .chip-unconfirmed { color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .tick { color: #7fd6a6; }
.card-focus .qmark { color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .warn { color: #ff9a88; }
.card-focus .btn { background: transparent; border-color: var(--focus-line); color: var(--focus-ink); }
.card-focus .btn:hover { border-color: var(--focus-muted); }
.card-focus .btn.primary { background: var(--lamp); border-color: var(--lamp); color: #23292a; }
.card-focus .dots i { background: var(--focus-line); }
.card-focus .dots i.done { background: transparent; }
.card-focus .dots i.on { background: var(--lamp); }
.card-focus code { color: var(--focus-ink); }

/* ---------- home ---------- */
.home { max-width: 760px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 64px 20px 80px; display: grid; gap: 18px; }
.home > .eyebrow { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink); }
.home > .eyebrow::before { content: ""; width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 7px; background: radial-gradient(circle, var(--lamp) 0 4.5px, transparent 5.5px), var(--ink); box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 transparent; flex: none; }
.home h1 { margin: 0; font-size: clamp(30px, 4.4vw, 42px); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.025em; line-height: 1.08; }
.lede { font-size: 16px; margin: 0; }
.home-ask { display: flex; gap: 8px; padding: 6px; background: var(--surface); border: 1.5px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 16px; }
.home-ask input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; border: 0; outline: none; border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 10px; font: inherit; font-size: 15.5px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink); }
.home-ask input:focus-visible { outline: none; }
.home-ask:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--lamp-glow); }
.home-ask .btn { border-radius: 11px; padding: 8px 18px; font-size: 14px; }
.section-title { font-size: 13px; margin: 22px 0 10px; color: var(--muted); font-weight: 600; }
.maplist { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 8px; }
.maplist li { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 14px; padding: 12px 16px; display: grid; gap: 2px; }
.maplist li:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.maplist a { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }
```

Direction A is now built into the viewer, and every feature still works; only where things sit and how they look changed. Typecheck passes, all 133 tests pass, and I clicked through it in the preview (scripted Claude on a copy of the care app): selecting a box, the walkthrough, asking a question, and the proposed fix with Approve and Reject. That last flow was real ask flow, so it also exercised the "Claude is working" progress and the answer's tabs and sources.

**Where things moved**
- **Top bar** keeps only the illuminate mark (it links home), the map switcher in the middle, a confirmed-claims bar with its count, New map, Stop and the connection dot.
- **Bottom dock** is new (`dock.tsx`). It has three groups:
  - **Walkthrough:** start it, step back and forward, see the current stop's title, leave it.
  - **Ask about the map:** the question box, with your selection riding along as chips.
  - **View:** zoom out, zoom in, and fit the whole map. These replace the top-bar zoom buttons and the React Flow controls in the corner.
- **Side panel** keeps all its cards. The card for what you're focused on (a walkthrough stop, an answer, or a selected box or arrow) is now dark like A's popover. Fixes, layers, history and progress stay as light cards.

**How it looks**
- **Canvas:** off-white with dots. Areas are soft rounded regions with plain labels instead of all-caps mono.
- **Boxes:** white cards with an ink outline, a larger title, and a code chip ticked when confirmed or marked "?" when not. Plain steps have no label; special kinds say what they are ("Where it starts", "Background job", and so on). They're bigger now (232×96, set in `layout.ts`), with a little more spacing so arrow labels fit.
- **Highlights:** what's lit, by the walkthrough or a selection, glows lamp yellow, and highlighted arrows turn dark ink.
- **Gaps** show the red "?" bubble beside the claim. A proposed fix shows as a green dashed arrow labelled "+ now listens".
- **Colours:** "Claude is working" changed from amber to violet, so it doesn't clash with the yellow.
- **Font:** Instrument Sans, added as a pinned npm package (`@fontsource-variable/instrument-sans@5.3.0`) so it loads locally rather than from Google.
- **Dark mode** has a matching palette, but I only looked at light mode.

**Two things to know**
- The walkthrough's Back/Next buttons are in both the dock and the walkthrough card in the panel. I kept both rather than remove a control; say if you want just one.
- The home page got the same type, a bordered ask box and the brand mark.

```typescript
// The walkthrough, as a bubble on the map: the stop's text and the buttons to move through it sit together, next to
// the boxes it lights up. The camera leaves room for it (see `TOUR_ROOM` in graph.tsx).
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

const cls = (...xs: (string | false | null | undefined)[]) => xs.filter(Boolean).join(' ');

export type TourBubbleProps = {
  map: CodeMap;
  stop: number;
  onTour: (stop: number | null) => void;
  /** Start a question about this stop in the question box. */
  onAsk: (text: string) => void;
};

export function TourBubble({ map, stop: i, onTour, onAsk }: TourBubbleProps) {
  const stop = map.tour[i];
  if (!stop) return null;
  const last = i === map.tour.length - 1;
  return (
    <section className="card card-focus tour-bubble" aria-label="Walkthrough" aria-live="polite">
      <button className="card-close" aria-label="Leave the walkthrough" title="Leave the walkthrough (Esc)" onClick={() => onTour(null)}>×</button>
      <div className="tour-head">
        <span className="eyebrow">Walkthrough, stop {i + 1} of {map.tour.length}</span>
        <span className="dots" aria-hidden="true">
          {map.tour.map((t, n) => <i key={t.id} className={cls(n === i && 'on', n < i && 'done')} />)}
        </span>
      </div>
      <h2 className="card-title">{stop.title}</h2>
      <p className="depth-text">{stop.text}</p>
      {stop.terms?.length ? <p className="muted small">Terms: {stop.terms.join(', ')}</p> : null}
      <div className="tour-nav">
        <button className="btn" disabled={i === 0} onClick={() => onTour(i - 1)}>‹ Back</button>
        <button className="btn" onClick={() => onAsk(`About “${stop.title}”: `)}>Ask about this step</button>
        <span className="grow" />
        {last
          ? <button className="btn primary" onClick={() => onTour(null)}>Done</button>
          : <button className="btn primary" onClick={() => onTour(i + 1)}>Next ›</button>}
      </div>
      <div className="kbd">← → to step, Esc to leave</div>
    </section>
  );
}

```

```typescript
// The panel's width: drag its left edge (or focus the edge and use the arrow keys). Remembered between visits.
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';

const KEY = 'illuminate-panel-width';
const MIN = 300;
const DEFAULT = 400;
/** Never squeeze the map narrower than this. */
const MAP_MIN = 360;

const clamp = (w: number) => Math.round(Math.max(MIN, Math.min(w, Math.max(MIN, window.innerWidth - MAP_MIN))));

export function usePanelWidth(): [number, (w: number) => void] {
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(() => {
    const saved = Number(localStorage.getItem(KEY));
    return clamp(saved > 0 ? saved : DEFAULT);
  });
  const set = useCallback((w: number) => {
    const next = clamp(w);
    setWidth(next);
    localStorage.setItem(KEY, String(next));
  }, []);
  // A smaller window can't keep a panel that leaves no room for the map.
  useEffect(() => {
    const onResize = () => setWidth((w) => clamp(w));
    window.addEventListener('resize', onResize);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', onResize);
  }, []);
  return [width, set];
}

/** The draggable left edge of the panel. The panel sits flush right, so its width is the distance to the window's edge. */
export function PanelResizer({ width, onWidth }: { width: number; onWidth: (w: number) => void }) {
  return (
    <div
      className="panel-handle"
      role="separator"
      aria-orientation="vertical"
      aria-label="Panel width"
      aria-valuenow={width}
      aria-valuemin={MIN}
      tabIndex={0}
      title="Drag to resize the panel"
      onPointerDown={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        const el = e.currentTarget;
        el.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
        document.body.classList.add('resizing');
        const move = (ev: PointerEvent) => onWidth(window.innerWidth - ev.clientX);
        const up = () => {
          el.removeEventListener('pointermove', move);
          el.removeEventListener('pointerup', up);
          el.removeEventListener('pointercancel', up);
          document.body.classList.remove('resizing');
        };
        el.addEventListener('pointermove', move);
        el.addEventListener('pointerup', up);
        el.addEventListener('pointercancel', up);
      }}
      onDoubleClick={() => onWidth(DEFAULT)}
      onKeyDown={(e) => {
        if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') { e.preventDefault(); onWidth(width + 24); }
        if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') { e.preventDefault(); onWidth(width - 24); }
      }}
    />
  );
}

```

_**User (2026-11-04 22:05:23Z)**_

do you think the record of questions is necessary? Idk if it would actually be useful or just adds space. whats the rationale. pros are it would help people go back to earlier questions but my thought process is maybe people will use this kind of as a conversation and not bother to look back

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-04 22:05:50Z)**_

I'd keep the ability to go back to earlier questions, but stop it from taking up space all the time. You're right that most people will treat this as a conversation and keep asking forward. The list isn't really there for browsing, though; it's the only way back to a few things that matter:

1. **Undo for an applied fix.** The Undo button lives on the answer that proposed the fix. Ask anything after approving a fix, and the earlier-questions list is the only route back to Undo.
2. **Saved and shared maps.** Answers are saved in the map file under `.illuminate/maps`. When you reopen a map, or a teammate opens one you committed, the questions already asked are often the most useful part ("someone already asked why the email is late"). Without the list, that saved conversation is invisible.
3. **Boxes that answers added.** The "Added by your questions" toggles (including "Show the original map") are in the same panel. If the panel only opens for an answer or a selection, those toggles become hard to reach too.

So the problem isn't the feature, it's that it forces the panel open. **My suggestion:** stop opening the panel just to show history, and put a small "Earlier questions (3)" button in the dock instead. It would open a little list where clicking a question brings its answer back into the panel, and the added-boxes toggles would sit in that same list. You get a full-width map by default, and the history is one click away when you need it.

The alternative is cutting it entirely. That's cleaner, but you'd lose Undo after asking a follow-up and the conversation on saved maps, and you'd want a different home for the layer toggles.

Want me to build the dock version?

```typescript
  const layers = layersOf(s);

  // Close on a click elsewhere, or on Esc (before Esc steps the map back a level).
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return;
    const onDown = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      if (!ref.current?.contains(e.target as Node)) setOpen(false);
    };
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
      e.stopPropagation();
      setOpen(false);
    };
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', onDown);
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey, true);
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onDown);
      document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey, true);
    };
  }, [open]);

  if (!s.answers.length) return null;
  const allHidden = layers.length > 0 && layers.every((l) => !l.visible);

  return (
    <section className="dock-part dock-history" aria-label="Earlier questions" ref={ref}>
      <h2 className="dock-title">History</h2>
      <button className={cls('dock-start', open && 'on')} aria-expanded={open} onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}>
        Earlier questions <span className="muted">{s.answers.length}</span>
      </button>
      {open && (
        <div className="history-pop" role="dialog" aria-label="Earlier questions">
          <ul className="history">
            {s.answers.slice().reverse().map((a) => (
              <li key={a.id}>
                <button
                  className={cls('history-q', a.id === s.shown && 'on')}
                  onClick={() => {
                    dispatch({ type: 'show', answerId: a.id });
                    setOpen(false);
                  }}
                >
                  {a.question}
                </button>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
          {layers.length > 0 && (
            <div className="history-layers">
              <h3 className="dock-title">Added by your questions</h3>
              <ul className="layers">
                {layers.map((l) => (
                  <li key={l.answerId}>
                    <label>
                      <input type="checkbox" checked={l.visible} onChange={(e) => dispatch({ type: 'layer', answerId: l.answerId, visible: e.target.checked })} />
                      <span className="layer-n">+{l.ids.length}</span>
                      <span className="layer-q" title={l.question}>{l.question}</span>
                    </label>
                  </li>
                ))}
              </ul>
              <div className="btns">
                <button className="btn" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'allLayers', visible: allHidden })}>{allHidden ? 'Show everything' : 'Show the original map'}</button>
              </div>
            </div>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

<pasted_content id="814e">
Concept
How it works
Code
Claude sends back a draft map, and then a loop runs. Each time through, codemap reads Claude's latest reply and checks every claim against the code. It remembers the version with the fewest failed claims. If anything failed, it sends Claude a list of what to correct and goes around again. After at most two correction rounds it stops and keeps the best version, which isn't always the newest one
</pasted_content id="814e">




<pasted_content id="814e">
How it works
Code
Each pass through the loop does five things:
1. **Read the reply.** The first reply is a whole map. Every later reply is a "patch", meaning just the changes. A patch is applied on top of `current`, the last map that could be read.
2. **If the reply can't be read** (wrong shape or invalid changes), codemap builds a repair request. If there's no readable map yet, it asks Claude to rewrite the whole map ("fix the map's structure"). Otherwise it asks Claude to correct its changes.
3. **If it can be read,** it becomes `current` and the checker re-reads the cited code. If this version has fewer unconfirmed claims than the best one so far, it becomes the new `best`. If any claims are unconfirmed, codemap builds a repair request listing exactly those claims, plus real function names to choose from.
4. **Stop or go again.** The loop ends when there's nothing to repair or the round limit is reached (`repairs`, 2 by default).
5. **Send the repair.** Otherwise the request goes back to Claude in the same session (`resume`), so Claude still remembers the code it read. The next reply is expected to be a whole map or a patch, depending on the request. Cost and the round count go up each time.

After the loop, codemap returns `best`. If no version could ever be read, making the map fails with the last problems listed.
</pasted_content id="814e">




<pasted_content id="814e">
Code
All of this is in `makeMap`, packages/server/src/maker.ts:
- **Loop start:** line 51, `for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++)`.
- **Reading the reply:** line 52 uses `parseMap` for a whole map, or `applyPatch` (lines 27–31, which wraps `patchMap`) for a patch.
- **Unreadable reply:** line 56 picks `shapeRepairPrompt` or `patchRepairPrompt`.
- **Check and best so far:** line 60 runs `check`, and line 61 updates `best`.
- **Failed claims:** line 63 builds `evidenceRepairPrompt`.
- **Exit:** line 65 stops when there's nothing to repair or `attempt >= (o.repairs ?? 2)`.
- **Repair round:** line 67 sends the request with `res.sessionId`, and line 68 sets the expected reply type.
- **Result:** line 73 returns `best`.
</pasted_content id="814e">

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-04 22:27:04Z)**_

The backend is already half a conversation. When you ask a follow-up, Claude gets your last three questions and their answers, and when it needs to read code it picks up the same session it used before. What makes it feel like one-off Q&A is the screen: each answer replaces the last one, and earlier ones are tucked away.

**Conversation or Q&A?** I'd go with a conversation. People don't ask one perfect question. They ask, read, then ask "wait, why?" or "what if this failed?". Treating each question as a fresh card makes every follow-up feel like starting over.

The risk is that it turns into Claude Code with a diagram attached: long prose that nobody checks. So I'd keep one rule: every reply points at the map. It lights up the boxes it's talking about, shows what it's based on, and anything it adds to the map still has to pass the checker. The map is what makes this different from Claude Code; the conversation is how you move around it.

**Why the three tabs feel unintuitive.** Your example shows it well:
- They aren't three answers to choose between. They're the same answer at three levels of detail, and you can't tell which level you want until you've read it.
- "Concept" and "How it works" don't tell you what you'll get.
- The Code tab is a list of line numbers you can't click.

What I'd do instead:
- Lead with the plain answer, a few sentences, no tab.
- Put a "Walk me through it" expander under it for the step-by-step version. This is already generated, so it opens instantly.
- Turn code references into chips like `maker.ts:51`. Clicking one lights up its box on the map and shows the line.
- Keep fixes appearing inline under the reply that proposed them, as now.

**What the screen would become.**
- **The panel is the conversation.** Your question, the reply, your next question, the next reply, and so on.
- **The ask box moves to the bottom of that thread** once a conversation is open. Otherwise you'd be typing in the dock and reading in the panel, which is the same split you disliked with the walkthrough. On a fresh map, the dock's ask box starts the conversation and the panel slides in.
- **The "Earlier questions" corner button goes away.** The thread is the history. The "Added by your questions" toggles would sit with the replies that added those boxes.

On the server side, this is mostly a change to how answers are shown. The one real change is giving Claude more of the conversation, and it should get the step-by-step parts too, not just the short answers.

Want me to mock up the conversation panel first so you can react to it, or go straight to building it?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-04 22:32:24Z)**_

Agreed, it shouldn't be a rule. Claude should decide whether a reply needs the map at all.

Here's how that decision works today. Before answering, a quick call to Claude with no access to the code looks at the map, the code around its citations and your last three questions. It picks a route:
- **answer:** the map is enough.
- **code:** it needs to read more of the code. This is also the only way it can add to the map or propose a fix.
- **elsewhere:** it's a different part of the app, so it offers a new map.

The prompt says "when in doubt, use code". Lighting up boxes is an optional extra on any answer.

The catch: **nothing checks whether that call is right.** The tests use a scripted Claude, so they check what happens once a route is picked, never whether it picked the right one. So here's what I'd do to keep the decisions accurate, most important first:

**1. Measure it.** Build a small labelled set: around 30–50 questions on the care-app map and a couple of this repo's own maps, each with the right call. For example:
- "what's an event bus?" → just words
- "why is the email late?" → read the code, light up the path
- "how does billing work?" → different part of the app

Run it against the real Claude with a command like `npm run eval:routing`, kept separate from `npm test` (which must never call a model). It would report which calls it got wrong. Without this, any prompt change is a guess. Real conversations will show which questions to add.

**2. Make the costly mistakes rare and the cheap ones easy to undo.** The mistakes aren't equally bad:
- **Answering from the map when it needed the code** is the worst. You get a confident answer about code it never read, which breaks the whole trust promise. Keep leaning against this.
- **Reading the code when it didn't need to** only costs time and money.
- **Adding boxes it didn't need** costs some clutter. It's checked, and you can hide it.
- **Offering a new map wrongly** costs nothing; you're asked first anyway.

Then show the call quietly on each reply with a way to override it: "Answered from the map · *Look in the code*", or "Added 2 boxes · *Hide*". A wrong call costs one click.

**3. Have the code catch it guessing.** The checker idea applies here too. If an answer from the map names functions or files that weren't in what Claude was shown, it's guessing about code it can't see. That's a simple, fast check against names we already have, so the reply could be sent to the code route automatically. Claude can't overrule it.

**4. Split one decision into two.** "code" currently means both "needs to read code" and "should draw on the map". With a conversation those come apart: "what does that function do?" needs code but no drawing. So:
- **Where to look:** map only, read the code, or a different part of the app.
- **How to show it:** just words, light up boxes, add to the map, or offer a new map.

Each is easier to judge on its own, and easier to measure in the eval. I'd also ask Claude for a one-line reason for each choice, which helps when an eval fails.

**5. Give it the whole conversation.** In a conversation, "show me that in the code" depends on what "that" was. Right now the quick call only sees your last three questions and their short answers.

I'd start with the eval set (1), because it tells you whether 2–5 actually help. Want me to start there?

```text
    '',
    ...EVIDENCE_RULES,
```

```typescript
// The side panel is the conversation about this map: each question, Claude's reply (the plain answer first, more on
// request), and under a reply whatever came with it (a fix to approve, the offer of a new map, boxes it added). Claude's
// progress shows at the end while it works, then what's selected, then the question box.
// (The walkthrough is a bubble on the map: tour.tsx. The button that reopens a closed conversation: history.tsx.)
import { useEffect, useRef, type Dispatch, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { pageUrl } from './api';
import { layersOf, type Action, type FixState, type State } from './state';
import type { Answer, CheckReport, ClaimCheck, CodeMap } from './types';

const cls = (...xs: (string | false | null | undefined)[]) => xs.filter(Boolean).join(' ');

/** A readable name for any id on the map. */
export function nameOf(map: CodeMap, id: string): string {
  const n = map.nodes.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (n) return n.name;
  const e = map.edges.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (e) return `${nameOf(map, e.from)} → ${nameOf(map, e.to)}`;
  const a = map.absences.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (a) return a.claim;
  const area = map.areas.find((x) => x.id === id);
  return area?.label ?? id;
}

function checkOf(report: CheckReport | null, id: string): ClaimCheck | { status: 'confirmed' | 'unconfirmed'; reasons: string[]; evidence?: never } | null {
  if (!report) return null;
  return report.nodes[id] ?? report.edges[id] ?? (report.absences[id] ? { status: report.absences[id]!.status, reasons: report.absences[id]!.reasons } : null);
}

function Card({ eyebrow, title, children, tone, className }: { eyebrow?: string; title?: ReactNode; children: ReactNode; tone?: 'ai' | 'ok' | 'dead' | 'focus'; className?: string }) {
  return (
    <section className={cls('card', tone && `card-${tone}`, className)}>
      {eyebrow && <div className="eyebrow">{eyebrow}</div>}
      {title && <h2 className="card-title">{title}</h2>}
      {children}
    </section>
  );
}

/** The plain answer, with the step-by-step and the code a click away rather than in tabs to choose between. */
function Explained({ concept, how, code }: { concept?: string; how?: string; code?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="explained">
      {concept?.trim() && <p className="depth-text">{concept}</p>}
      {how?.trim() && (
        <details className="more">
          <summary>Walk me through it</summary>
          <div className="depth-text">{how}</div>
        </details>
      )}
      {code?.trim() && (
        <details className="more">
          <summary>Show the code</summary>
          <div className="depth-text mono">{code}</div>
        </details>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

function Chips({ map, ids, onPick }: { map: CodeMap; ids: { id: string; status: string }[]; onPick: (id: string) => void }) {
  if (!ids.length) return null;
  return (
    <div className="chips">
      {ids.map(({ id, status }) => (
        <button key={id} className={cls('chip', status !== 'confirmed' && 'chip-unconfirmed')} onClick={() => onPick(id)} title={status === 'confirmed' ? 'Confirmed against the code' : "Couldn't confirm against the code"}>
          <span className={status === 'confirmed' ? 'tick' : 'qmark'}>{status === 'confirmed' ? '✓' : '?'}</span>
          {nameOf(map, id)}
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

function Progress({ lines, working }: { lines: string[]; working: boolean }) {
  const shown = lines.slice(-8);
  return (
    <ul className="progress">
      {shown.map((l, i) => (
        <li key={`${i}-${l}`} className={cls(working && i === shown.length - 1 && 'running')}>
          <span className="ic">{working && i === shown.length - 1 ? '…' : '✓'}</span>
          {l}
        </li>
      ))}
      {!shown.length && working && <li className="running"><span className="ic">…</span>Starting</li>}
    </ul>
  );
}

function FixCard({ fix, onApprove, onReject, onUndo, map }: { fix: FixState; map: CodeMap; onApprove: () => void; onReject: () => void; onUndo: () => void }) {
  const p = fix.proposal;
  const dirty = p.files.filter((f) => f.uncommitted);
  if (fix.status === 'applied') {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow="Fix applied · re-checked" tone="ok">
        <ul className="progress">
          <li><span className="ic">✓</span>Changed {p.files.length} {p.files.length === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'}: {p.files.map((f) => f.file).join(', ')}</li>
          {fix.edgeId && <li><span className="ic">✓</span>New confirmed connection: {nameOf(map, fix.edgeId)}</li>}
          {fix.closed.length > 0 && <li><span className="ic">✓</span>Closed: {fix.closed.length === 1 ? 'the missing connection' : `${fix.closed.length} missing connections`}</li>}
        </ul>
        {fix.undoable
          ? <div className="btns"><button className="btn" onClick={onUndo}>Undo this fix</button></div>
          : <p className="muted small">Undo ended when illuminate stopped. Use git to reverse it.</p>}
      </Card>
    );
  }
  if (fix.status === 'rejected' || fix.status === 'undone') {
    return <Card eyebrow={fix.status === 'undone' ? 'Fix undone' : 'Fix rejected'}><p className="muted">{p.summary}</p>{fix.status === 'undone' && <div className="btns"><button className="btn" onClick={onApprove}>Apply it again</button></div>}</Card>;
  }
  return (
    <Card eyebrow={`Proposed fix · ${p.files.length} ${p.files.length === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'} · nothing changed yet`} tone="ai">
      <p>{p.summary}</p>
      {p.connects && <p className="muted small">The green dashed arrow is the connection it adds.</p>}
      <pre className="diff">{p.diff.split('\n').map((l, i) => <span key={i} className={l.startsWith('+ ') ? 'add' : l.startsWith('- ') ? 'del' : l.includes(' · ') ? 'file' : ''}>{l}{'\n'}</span>)}</pre>
      {dirty.length > 0 ? (
        <p className="warn small">⚠ {dirty.map((f) => f.file).join(', ')} {dirty.length === 1 ? 'has' : 'have'} uncommitted changes. They'll be kept; the fix applies on top.</p>
      ) : null}
      {fix.problems.length > 0 && <ul className="problems">{fix.problems.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ul>}
      <div className="btns">
        <button className="btn primary" disabled={fix.status === 'applying'} onClick={onApprove}>{fix.status === 'applying' ? 'Applying…' : 'Approve'}</button>
        <button className="btn" onClick={onReject}>Reject</button>
      </div>
      <p className="muted small">Won't apply if these files change first.</p>
    </Card>
  );
}

export type PanelProps = {
  state: State;
  dispatch: Dispatch<Action>;
  onFix: (fixId: string, action: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'undo') => void;
  onFocus: (id: string) => void;
  onOffer: (answerId: string, choice: 'map' | 'words') => void;
  /** The question box, at the bottom of the conversation. */
  composer: ReactNode;
};

export function Panel({ state: s, dispatch, onFix, onFocus, onOffer, composer }: PanelProps) {
  const map = s.map;
  const job = s.job;
  const scroller = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  // Keep the newest turn in view as the conversation grows and while Claude works.
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = scroller.current;
    if (el) el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
  }, [s.answers.length, job?.progress.length, !!job]);

  if (s.phase === 'loading') return <aside className="panel"><div className="panel-scroll"><Card><p className="muted">Loading…</p></Card></div></aside>;
  if (s.phase === 'missing') return <aside className="panel"><div className="panel-scroll"><Card title="No map here"><p className="muted">This map isn't in this repo.</p></Card></div></aside>;
  if (!map) {
    return (
      <aside className="panel">
        <div className="panel-scroll">
          {job && (
            <Card eyebrow="Making your map" title={job.question} tone="ai">
              <Progress lines={job.progress} working />
            </Card>
          )}
          {s.phase === 'failed' && <Card title="The map couldn't be made" tone="dead"><p>{s.error}</p></Card>}
        </div>
      </aside>
    );
  }

  const selected = [...s.selection.nodes, ...s.selection.edges, ...s.selection.absences];
  const layers = layersOf(s);
  const allHidden = layers.length > 0 && layers.every((l) => !l.visible);

  return (
    <aside className="panel" aria-label="Conversation about this map">
      <header className="panel-head">
        <h2 className="panel-title">Conversation</h2>
        {layers.length > 0 && (
          <button className="link-btn small" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'allLayers', visible: allHidden })}>{allHidden ? 'Show everything' : 'Show the original map'}</button>
        )}
        <button className="card-close" aria-label="Close the conversation" title="Close (Esc). It stays here to reopen." onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'overview' })}>×</button>
      </header>

      <div className="panel-scroll" ref={scroller}>
        {s.error && <div className="banner banner-dead" role="alert">{s.error}<button className="link-btn" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'error', message: null })}>Dismiss</button></div>}

        {s.answers.map((a) => (
          <Turn key={a.id} answer={a} state={s} dispatch={dispatch} onFix={onFix} onFocus={onFocus} onOffer={onOffer} />
        ))}

        {job?.kind === 'ask' && (
          <article className="turn">
            <You question={job.question} />
            <Card eyebrow="Claude is working" tone="ai">
              <Progress lines={job.progress} working />
            </Card>
          </article>
        )}

        {!s.answers.length && !job && !selected.length && <p className="muted small thread-empty">Ask anything about this map. Click a box or arrow first to ask about it.</p>}
      </div>

      <footer className="panel-foot">
        {selected.length > 0 && <Selected map={map} report={s.report} ids={selected} />}
        {composer}
      </footer>
    </aside>
  );
}

/** Your side of a turn: the question. */
function You({ question, about }: { question: string; about?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="you">
      <p className="you-q">{question}</p>
      {about && <span className="you-about">About {about}</span>}
    </div>
  );
}

/** One question and everything that came back for it. */
function Turn({ answer: a, state: s, dispatch, onFix, onFocus, onOffer }: { answer: Answer; state: State; dispatch: Dispatch<Action>; onFix: PanelProps['onFix']; onFocus: (id: string) => void; onOffer: PanelProps['onOffer'] }) {
  const map = s.map!;
  const fix = a.fix ? s.fixes[a.fix.id] ?? null : null;
  const lit = a.id === s.shown;
  const about = [...(a.selection.nodes ?? []), ...(a.selection.edges ?? []), ...(a.selection.absences ?? [])].map((id) => nameOf(map, id)).join(', ');
  const layer = layersOf(s).find((l) => l.answerId === a.id);
  const fixProblems = a.problems.filter((x) => x.startsWith('The proposed fix'));
  const otherProblems = a.problems.filter((x) => !x.startsWith('The proposed fix'));
  // Sources as the map is now: drop what a later fix removed, and show each one's current status.
  const refs = a.refs.filter((r) => r.status !== 'unknown' && checkOf(s.report, r.id)).map((r) => ({ id: r.id, status: checkOf(s.report, r.id)!.status }));
  const onMap = a.moves.highlight.length > 0 || !!a.moves.focus || a.added.length > 0;

  return (
    <article className="turn">
      <You question={a.question} about={about || undefined} />
      {a.offer ? (
        <OfferCard answer={a} busy={!!s.job} onOffer={onOffer} />
      ) : (
        <section className={cls('card', 'reply', lit && 'card-focus')}>
          <div className="reply-meta">
            <span>{a.source === 'map' ? 'From the map' : 'Looked in the code'}</span>
            {onMap && (lit
              ? <span className="reply-lit">Lit on the map</span>
              : <button className="link-btn small" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'show', answerId: a.id })}>Show on the map</button>)}
          </div>
          <Explained concept={a.concept} how={a.how} code={a.code} />
          {refs.length > 0 && <div className="basis"><div className="eyebrow">Based on</div><Chips map={map} ids={refs} onPick={onFocus} /></div>}
          {layer && (
            <div className="reply-added">
              <span>Added {layer.ids.length} to the map</span>
              <button className="link-btn small" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'layer', answerId: a.id, visible: !layer.visible })}>{layer.visible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}</button>
            </div>
          )}
          {otherProblems.length > 0 && (
            <details className="problems-box"><summary>{otherProblems.length} thing{otherProblems.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} Claude found but couldn't confirm</summary><ul className="problems">{otherProblems.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ul></details>
          )}
        </section>
      )}
      {fix && <FixCard fix={fix} map={map} onApprove={() => onFix(fix.proposal.id, 'approve')} onReject={() => onFix(fix.proposal.id, 'reject')} onUndo={() => onFix(fix.proposal.id, 'undo')} />}
      {fixProblems.length > 0 && (
        <Card eyebrow="The proposed fix can't be applied" tone="dead"><ul className="problems">{fixProblems.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x.replace('The proposed fix can\'t be applied: ', '')}</li>)}</ul><p className="muted small">Ask again, or ask for a smaller change.</p></Card>
      )}
    </article>
  );
}

/** "This looks like a different part of the app": a new map for it (or the one that already covers it), or words. */
function OfferCard({ answer, busy, onOffer }: { answer: Answer; busy: boolean; onOffer: (answerId: string, choice: 'map' | 'words') => void }) {
  const o = answer.offer!;
  if (o.status === 'mapped') {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow="A different part of the app">
        <p className="muted">You made a new map for this.</p>
        {o.mapId && <div className="btns"><a className="btn primary" href={pageUrl(o.mapId)}>Open it</a></div>}
      </Card>
    );
  }
  if (o.status === 'answered') {
    return <Card eyebrow="A different part of the app"><p className="muted">Answered in words, below.</p></Card>;
  }
  return (
    <Card eyebrow="A different part of the app" tone="ai">
      <p>This is about a different part of the app than this map shows.</p>
      {o.existing && <p>There's already a map for it: “{o.existing.question}”.</p>}
      <div className="btns">
        {o.existing && <a className="btn primary" href={pageUrl(o.existing.id)}>Open that map</a>}
        <button className={o.existing ? 'btn' : 'btn primary'} onClick={() => onOffer(answer.id, 'map')}>Make a new map for this</button>
        <button className="btn" disabled={busy} onClick={() => onOffer(answer.id, 'words')} title={busy ? 'Claude is still working on this map' : undefined}>Just answer in words</button>
      </div>
    </Card>
  );
}

/** What's selected: what your next question will be about, with what the map says about it. */
function Selected({ map, report, ids }: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport | null; ids: string[] }) {
  if (ids.length > 1) {
    return (
      <Card eyebrow={`Asking about ${ids.length} things`} className="card-selected">
        <Chips map={map} ids={ids.map((id) => ({ id, status: checkOf(report, id)?.status ?? 'unknown' }))} onPick={() => undefined} />
      </Card>
    );
  }
  const id = ids[0]!;
  const node = map.nodes.find((n) => n.id === id);
  const edge = map.edges.find((e) => e.id === id);
  const gap = map.absences.find((a) => a.id === id);
  const c = checkOf(report, id);
  const evidence = node?.evidence ?? edge?.evidence ?? [];
  const evidenceChecks = c && 'evidence' in c && c.evidence ? c.evidence : [];
  return (
    <Card eyebrow={node ? 'Step' : edge ? 'Connection' : 'Missing connection'} title={nameOf(map, id)} tone={gap ? 'dead' : undefined} className="card-selected">
      {node?.explain && <Explained {...node.explain} />}
      {gap && <p>Nothing in the code connects these. Searching <code>{gap.search.pattern}</code>{gap.search.paths ? <> in <code>{gap.search.paths.join(', ')}</code></> : null}: {report?.absences[gap.id]?.found ?? '?'} {report?.absences[gap.id]?.found === 1 ? 'match' : 'matches'}.</p>}
      {c && c.status !== 'confirmed' && <div className="warn small">Couldn't confirm against the code: {c.reasons.join('; ')}</div>}
      {evidence.length > 0 && (
        <div className="basis">
          <div className="eyebrow">In the code</div>
          <div className="chips">
            {evidence.map((e, i) => {
              const ok = evidenceChecks[i]?.ok ?? false;
              return <span key={i} className={cls('chip static', !ok && 'chip-unconfirmed')}><span className={ok ? 'tick' : 'qmark'}>{ok ? '✓' : '?'}</span>{e.file}:{evidenceChecks[i]?.foundAt ?? e.line}</span>;
            })}
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </Card>
  );
}
```

```text
// The dock floating along the bottom of the map: the way into the walkthrough and the question box. Everything you do
// to the map itself lives here, so the top bar only says which map this is. (Zoom is the mouse wheel or trackpad.)
// While the walkthrough runs, its controls are in the bubble beside its text (tour.tsx), so the dock only asks.
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

export type DockProps = {
  map: CodeMap;
  /** The walkthrough stop on screen, or null when the walkthrough isn't running. */
  tour: number | null;
  onTour: (stop: number | null) => void;
  /** How many boxes, arrows and gaps are selected (the hint changes once something is). */
  selected: number;
  /** The question box (the composer). */
  children: ReactNode;
};

export function Dock({ map, tour, onTour, selected, children }: DockProps) {
  const stops = map.tour.length;
  return (
    <div className="dock">
      {stops > 0 && tour === null && (
        <section className="dock-part dock-walk" aria-label="Walkthrough">
          <h2 className="dock-title">Walkthrough</h2>
          <button className="dock-start" onClick={() => onTour(0)}>
            Take the walkthrough <span className="muted">{stops} {stops === 1 ? 'stop' : 'stops'}</span>
          </button>
        </section>
      )}
      <section className="dock-part dock-ask" aria-label="Ask about the map">
        <div className="dock-head">
          <h2 className="dock-title">Ask about the map</h2>
          <span className="dock-hint">{selected ? 'Shift-click to add more' : 'Click a box or arrow to ask about it'}</span>
        </div>
        {children}
      </section>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The panel is now a conversation instead of one answer at a time, and Claude decides per reply whether to light up the map, as you wanted. I ran a three-question conversation in the preview (a plain answer, a follow-up that read the code and added boxes, then one that proposed a fix), and reopened it after a reload. Typecheck passes, and all 135 tests pass, including two new ones.

**What it looks like**
- **Turns in order.** Each question is a bubble on the right. If you'd selected something, it says what the question was about.
- **Replies.** Each reply leads with the plain answer. "Walk me through it" and "Show the code" open underneath instead of being tabs.
- **What came with a reply sits under it:** its fix card (so Approve and Undo stay with it), its "different part of the app" offer, and "Added 2 to the map · Hide".
- **The reply lit on the map is the dark one.** Older replies have "Show on the map", which lights their path again.
- **Claude's progress** appears in the conversation under your question while it works, and the conversation scrolls to keep the newest turn in view.

**One question box.** While the conversation is open, the box is at its bottom and takes focus. When it's closed, the box is back in the dock. What you've selected shows just above the box, as context for your next question.

**Opening and closing.**
- The conversation opens when you ask, select something, or Claude is working.
- × or Esc closes it, and the map goes back to full width.
- A "Conversation 3" button in the map's top-left corner reopens it at the latest reply.
- "Show the original map" moved to the conversation's header.

**Claude gets the conversation.** Both steps (the quick map-only one and the one that reads code) now see the last six turns, each with a short version of its step-by-step answer. That's so "show me that in the code" knows what "that" was. Before, only the quick step saw anything: the last three short answers.

Changes are mostly in `panel.tsx`. The corner button is in `history.tsx`, and the server change is in `prompts.ts` and `server.ts`. CLAUDE.md has a new "Conversation" note.

Some things you'll probably want to judge in use:
- **Long conversations get tall.** Each reply shows its "Based on" chips, so after a few turns there's a lot of scrolling. You could collapse older replies to just the answer.
- **The fix's green arrow only shows while its reply is the lit one.** That's how it worked before, but in a thread you can see the fix card while a different reply is lit and the arrow is gone.
- **Routing is untouched.** Claude still picks map, code or different-area exactly as before. The eval we talked about is the way to find out how often that call is wrong.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-05 00:52:11Z)**_

Mostly no. I'd drop the "Based on" chips, with one exception.

**Why they're mostly redundant.** A reply that relies on parts of the map already lights those parts up, and each box on the map already shows its ✓ and the code it comes from. So the map is the citation. The chips repeat what's lit, in a list below it, and they're a big part of why the conversation gets tall. They also cite map boxes, not the code itself; that's what "Show the code" is for.

**Where I'd stop the Claude Code comparison.** In Claude Code you're the developer: if you doubt something, you open the file. The people illuminate is for are reading code they didn't write and can't easily check, which is why the checker exists at all. So the trust signal matters more here than in Claude Code. It just doesn't need to be a list on every reply, because the map already shows it.

**The exception.** It's worth saying something when a reply rests on a claim the checker couldn't confirm. Today that only shows as a "?" chip, easy to miss among the ✓ ones. I'd replace the chips with a single line that appears only in that case: "Relies on 1 thing the checker couldn't confirm: *Queue the email*". Clicking the name would show it on the map. Most replies would show nothing.

Claude would still return what a reply is based on behind the scenes; that's what the "couldn't confirm" line is built from. Only the chips go. Want me to make that change?

<pasted_content id="814e">
do we prompt engineer specifically what you're saying right now w/ the responses?

From the map
Show on the map
Yes. The style of this reply comes from instructions codemap sends with each question, so it isn't left to chance. They ask for a short, plain-language summary with no jargon (this part), then a section on how it works, then the function and file names, and links to the boxes the answer relies on. Codemap also fixes the shape of the reply, so it can use specific parts of it, like which boxes to highlight on the map.

Walk me through it
When you ask a follow-up, the server runs `answer` (the 'Claude answers or offers' box). That function builds a prompt, meaning the written instructions plus the material sent to Claude. The prompt includes the map's JSON, which boxes you selected, your question, the lines of code the map cites, the last 6 turns of this conversation, and the names of up to 30 other maps in this repo. The instructions I received for this turn spell out the house style: 2–4 pln sentences for the summary, define any term you use, and so on. They also give three ways to handle a question: answer it, pass it on for a full read of the code, or offer a new map. Claude has to reply in a fixed structure (structured JSON). The server reads that reply with `RawAnswer.safeParse` and rejects it if the shape is wrong. It also checks the 'moves' (which box to focus on and which to highlight) and drops any that point to boxes not on the map. _**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-05 01:12:46Z)**_

Mostly no. I'd drop both, and also stop asking Claude to write them, not just hide them.

**"Walk me through it"** has little value. As your example shows, it mostly repeats the plain answer at more length. Its one real use is giving Claude context for follow-ups, but the plain answers cover most of that. And when Claude reads code for a follow-up, it continues the same session, so it remembers what it read anyway.

**"Show the code"** has some value for a developer who wants to jump to a file. But the map already does that: every box carries its function name and file:line, and clicking a box shows "In the code" with each line checked. So the visual already covers it. For the rare answer about code that isn't on the map, Claude can name the function in the answer itself.

**The bigger win is speed.** Today every reply writes three versions of itself, and the longer two are most of the writing, so replies are slower and cost more. Boxes are the same: the map maker writes all three versions for every box. Writing the map is already most of the time it takes to make one, so asking only for the plain version should make new maps noticeably faster.

What I'd do:
- **Prompts:** ask for only the plain answer, and only the plain explanation per box. I'd also tighten the answer guidance to keep it short and say what's lit, since the map does the explaining.
- **Viewer:** show just that text and remove "Walk me through it" and "Show the code".
- **Map format:** leave it alone. Those fields stay optional, so saved maps that have them still load (they just won't be shown). No change to `format.ts`.

Two other things in your example that this won't fix, but are worth knowing:
1. **"Added 5 to the map" on a question about how the screen works.** That's Claude choosing to draw when it should have just answered: the routing call we discussed. The eval would catch it.
2. **The first reply talked about its own instructions** ("The instructions I received for this turn…"). It's your repo, so that's fair game here, but the prompt should tell Claude to explain the code, not its own instructions.

Want me to go ahead with the prompts, the viewer and the box explanations?

```text
// What the model must return, as JSON Schema for structured output. Derived from the map format's zod schemas, so the
// two can't drift. Output is still validated with zod (and the map with `parseMap`) after it comes back.
import { z } from 'zod';
import { Absence, Area, CodeMap, Edge, Node } from '@illuminate/core';

/** Keywords some structured-output validators reject; zod and `parseMap` enforce them after the fact anyway. */
const STRIP = new Set(['$schema', '$id', 'pattern', 'default', 'format']);

function sanitize(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(sanitize);
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) if (!STRIP.has(k)) out[k] = sanitize(v);
  return out;
}

export function toSchema(schema: z.ZodType): Record<string, unknown> {
  return sanitize(z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: 'input' })) as Record<string, unknown>;
}

export const RawFix = z.object({
  summary: z.string().min(1).max(600),
  /** Exact-text replacements: `find` is copied from the file and occurs exactly once. */
  edits: z.array(z.object({ file: z.string().min(1), find: z.string().min(1), replace: z.string() })).max(12).default([]),
  creates: z.array(z.object({ file: z.string().min(1), content: z.string() })).max(6).default([]),
  /** The connection the fix creates between two boxes; `evidenceText` must appear in the new code. */
  connects: z
    .object({ from: z.string(), to: z.string(), label: z.string().min(1).max(60), evidenceFile: z.string().min(1), evidenceText: z.string().min(1).max(200) })
    .optional(),
});

export const RawAnswer = z.object({
  concept: z.string().min(1),
  how: z.string().default(''),
  code: z.string().default(''),
  /** Ids of the boxes, arrows and missing connections the answer relies on. */
  refs: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
  /** New things found while exploring, with evidence, same rules as the map. */
  add: z
    .object({ areas: z.array(Area).optional(), nodes: z.array(Node).optional(), edges: z.array(Edge).optional(), absences: z.array(Absence).optional() })
  ].join('\n');
}

export type SelectionLine = { id: string; label: string };

/** The map, what the checker couldn't confirm, what they selected and their question: shared by both answer prompts. */
function questionContext(map: CodeMap, report: CheckReport, selection: readonly SelectionLine[], question: string): string[] {
  const unconfirmed = [
    ...Object.entries(report.nodes), ...Object.entries(report.edges), ...Object.entries(report.absences),
  ].filter(([, c]) => c.status !== 'confirmed').map(([id]) => id);
  return [
    '## The map (JSON)',
    JSON.stringify(map),
    unconfirmed.length ? `\nThe checker could not confirm: ${unconfirmed.join(', ')}. Don\'t rely on those without checking.` : '\nThe checker confirmed every claim in the map.',
    '',
    selection.length ? `## They selected\n${selection.map((s) => `- ${s.id}: ${s.label}`).join('\n')}` : '## They selected nothing (the question is about the whole map)',
    '',
    `## Their question\n"${question}"`,
  ];
}

const ANSWER_DEPTHS = [
  '- `concept`: 2–4 plain sentences, no jargon. `how`: the mechanism; define any term you use. `code`: function names, files and lines.',
  '- `refs`: ids of the boxes, arrows and absences your answer relies on.',
];
```

```text
## 4. What the user wants from the interface (direct feedback)

- **Point at anything and ask.** Select a box, an arrow or a region; answers appear next to what was selected.
- **Plain English first.** Translating code into concepts *is* the value. Three depths: Concept, How it works, Code.
  Define jargon. Use a small concrete example from their own code.
- **A real graph:** areas as containers, steps inside, labeled arrows between them. An early design with lane rows of
  blocks was rejected as "unintuitive, not an actual graph".
2. **Check every claim.** `check()` re-reads each cited line, verifies calls, requests and imports against code facts,
   and re-runs the search behind every "nothing does X". Claude gets up to two rounds to fix what didn't hold. Anything
   still unconfirmed is shown with a "?", never hidden.
3. **Explore.** The viewer draws areas, steps, labeled arrows and red dashed gaps, with a walkthrough Claude wrote. Select
   anything and ask: answers come at three depths (concept, how it works, code) with their sources. Claude explores
   further when the map isn't enough; what it finds is drawn only if it passes the checker.
4. **Fix from the map.** Ask for a change and Claude proposes a fix, drawn as a green dashed arrow next to the exact diff.
   Nothing changes until you approve. Then illuminate writes exactly that change (refusing if the files changed since),
   re-checks the map, and offers Undo.
```
